articles.title: More than the Score - Manchester City: What does the Premier League do now? - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: What could the consequences of the Manchester City verdict be?
articles.body:
World Service , · 07 Oct 2026 , · 26 mins

An independent commission has found Manchester City guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations across a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018. During the period in question, City spent around $1.5 billion on transfers and won eight trophies - including three Premier League titles - but the club was found to have artificially inflated revenue through "sham" sponsorship agreements. City have always protested their innocence, and have lodged an appeal. In a short statement, they said the commission's ruling contained "clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe". So just how damaging could this case be for both Manchester City and the Premier League, and how does it compare to some of sport's other major scandals? More than the Score's Delyth Lloyd is joined by Kieran Maguire, professor of football finance at the University of Liverpool, and Simon Chadwick, professor of Afro-Eurasian sport at Emlyon Business School, to discuss the case and its potential consequences - as well as how far its impact could extend beyond football. Unexpected questions and beyond the scoresheet chat. More than the Score tells stories from all over the world of sport. From Formula One to netball, MMA to figure skating, and Grand Slam tennis to Diamond League athletics. We've got interviews with extraordinary athletes, as well as the experts working behind the scenes, from football super-agents to the coaches keeping athletes in peak form. Plus, we've got the expertise of the BBC's top journalists, who share their insights from decades of covering sport at all levels. articles.title: As potential Hurricane Isaias forms in the Gulf, Alabama says its game vs. Georgia is currently set to be played as scheduled
articles.summary: The top-10 matchup is set for a 7:30 p.m. ET kickoff. And right now, it looks like a lot of rain is in the forecast.
articles.body:
Alabama said Tuesday evening that its game against Georgia was set to proceed as scheduled.

A weather system in the Gulf of Mexico is virtually certain to become Tropical Storm Isaias , and maybe even a hurricane in the coming days. The track of the storm is currently aimed east of Texas and potentially toward the Gulf Coast of Mississippi and Alabama with potential landfall later in the week.

That means the No. 6 Crimson Tide's home game in Tuscaloosa against the No. 2 Bulldogs on Saturday could be plagued by lots and lots of rain.

"Alabama athletics is closely monitoring the weather forecast ahead of Saturday's football game vs. Georgia," a statement from the school said. "At this time, there are no plans to alter the contest. We will continue to observe conditions throughout the week and remain in communication with the Southeastern Conference office, as needed."

Alabama's statement came hours after Al.com published a story interviewing meteorologist James Spann, the most widely respected weather voice in the state.

"We've got potential for a hurricane making landfall in Mobile Bay," Spann told the site. "The Alabama-Georgia game, a presidential visit, 'College GameDay.' You got the big [Zach Bryan] concert at Auburn. This is the National Shrimp Festival at Gulf Shores this weekend, which is huge. I mean you could not … it's gonna be a nightmare."

Yes, Spann is referring to President Donald Trump. The president is expected to be in attendance for the game. It's the second SEC game he's attended in three weeks. He was at Texas' win over Tennessee in Week 4. ESPN's pregame show was also in Knoxville for that game.

Kickoff for Saturday's game is set for just after 7:30 p.m. ET on ABC. It's the only matchup of top-10 teams and one of just two matchups between teams in the AP Top 25 in Week 6.

articles.title: Lionel Messi's last game for Argentina: Pregame tears, a giant flying jersey and 1 final international goal
articles.summary: Messi scored or assisted on each of Argentina's 3 goals in a fitting coda to his international career.
articles.body:
Lionel Messi played his final World Cup game for Argentina in July. On Tuesday, at Buenos Aires' Estadio Monumental, the soccer icon played his last international match of any kind .

Tuesday's friendly between Argentina and Benin turned into an emotional farewell and a chance for a nation that adores Messi to celebrate its hero one last time on the field. And Messi, at the end, could not pretend it was anything else.

"Not coming back is going to hurt so much," Messi said postgame. "I swear I'd like to keep coming for the rest of my life, because playing for the Argentina national team is the most beautiful thing that can happen to you."

The match also featured two more assists and one last international goal from Messi, who played a part in each of Argentina's goals in a 3-0 win.

Messi's finale is cause for celebration across Argentina

The celebration started long before game time. In Rosario, about 185 miles northwest of Buenos Aires, a helicopter towed a massive replica of Messi's No. 10 Argentina jersey around the city.

Back in Buenos Aires, there were tears before the festivities had a chance to start. As Argentina's team bus arrived at the stadium, cameras captured Messi in tears on his final pregame ride with his teammates.

Once inside the stadium, Messi and the Argentina crowd were filled with emotion as the national anthem played.

At the song's conclusion, fireworks launched from around another giant replica of Messi's jersey at midfield.

Once the game began, not much time passed before another tribute ensued.

Play stopped at the 10-minute mark for more fireworks and an in-game celebration that featured an extended standing ovation and a moment for Benin players to pay their respects directly to Messi.

But Messi's day wasn't done. Fans didn't show up just to watch him play for 10 minutes. And he provided the home crowd with plenty of thrills throughout the game.

Messi delivered an on-target free kick in the 26th minute that Benin goaltender Marcel Dandjinou denied.

Minutes later, he got off another shot in transition that was also turned back by Dandjinou.

After halftime, Messi gave the fans what they showed up for with two assists and the final goal in Argentina's 3-0 win.

Messi contributes to all 3 Argentina goals

With the game in a scoreless tie, Messi delivered a corner kick from the left side in the 48th minute. The pass found Nicolás Otamendi, who powered the ball into the top of the net with his right foot for a 1-0 Argentina lead.

Minutes later, Messi delivered with another assist.

This time, he found Nico Paz just outside the box from the right sideline. Paz converted with a bending left-footer that snuck between Dandjinou and the goal post for a 2-0 Argentina lead in the 61st minute.

Then in the 71st minute, Messi had the opportunity to put the ball in the net himself. A foul in the box set Argentina up for a penalty.

Who else but Messi would take it? Messi lined up and delivered with a left-footed strike that had Dandjinou diving in the wrong direction.

Messi's teammates swarmed and embraced him as they savored the moment in front of a stadium-wide standing ovation. And he remained in the game until the final whistle.

Messi had one last chance to add to his tally with a free kick in extra time that he sent high above the net. But the miss did little to dampen what added up to a fitting coda to a spectacular international career.

When it was done, the game official handed Messi all the yellow and red cards in his pocket as a souvenir from his final game. And Messi shared hugs and handshakes with his teammates and Benin opponents.

The party was far from done, and fans remained in the stands to take in the postgame festivities. A drone show celebrated Messi's and Argentina's World Cup win from 2022.

Messi then took the mic to address fans one last time as a member of Argentina's national team.

articles.title: Lionel Messi's emotional farewell ends in one goal, two assists and a 3-0 win for Argentina over Benin
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Lionel Messi’s final appearance for Argentina ended with victory, emotion and one last unforgettable night at the Monumental as the South
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Lionel Messi’s final appearance for Argentina ended with victory, emotion and one last unforgettable night at the Monumental as the South American side defeated Benin 3-0 on Wednesday.The occasion was as much about Messi as the result. The stadium was packed long before kick-off, with the Argentine captain receiving an extraordinary farewell.Fabio Santana, a Malvinas War veteran and singer, performed the Argentine national anthem as Messi stood alongside his children, visibly emotional. A giant Messi shirt covered the pitch before the crowd erupted into a rendition of “Muchachos”.At the 10-minute mark, the match paused for another tribute, with every Benin player taking the opportunity to shake Messi’s hand.Argentina dominated possession early and repeatedly tried to find their captain in dangerous positions. Messi came close with a free-kick from outside the box, but Benin’s goalkeeper made a fine save.Lautaro Martínez also threatened after a run into the area, while another Messi pass nearly released him into space. Benin, however, refused to sit back completely and gradually grew into the contest.They eventually switched to a back five, with Messi receiving close attention whenever he came near the penalty area.As it happened: Argentina vs Benin HighlightsMessi's assist prompts openerThe breakthrough finally arrived shortly after half-time. Julián Álvarez won a corner after bursting down the left, and Messi delivered the set-piece perfectly.Nicolás Otamendi, left completely unmarked, volleyed home to put Argentina ahead. It was a fitting goal for the veteran defender, who was also making his final appearance for the national team.Argentina doubled their advantage through Nico Paz. The youngster, who had just come onto the pitch as a substitute, collected the ball and produced a beautiful left-footed curling finish, drawing comparisons with Messi’s trademark style.Messi on the scoresheetMessi was involved again, providing the assist as Paz announced himself on the biggest stage.Then came the moment everyone inside the Monumental had been waiting for. Messi stepped up from the penalty spot and calmly sent the goalkeeper the wrong way, placing the ball into the top-right corner for 3-0.There was still time for one final glimpse of magic. Messi had a late effort saved before another strike hit the post, and in the dying seconds he won a free-kick in his familiar range. He took responsibility one last time, but the effort sailed over the crossbar.The whistle confirmed Argentina’s 3-0 victory. For Messi, though, the scoreline was almost secondary. articles.title: USMNT grinds out 1-0 win over Canada to complete perfect 4-game window
articles.summary: Justin Ellis opened the USMNT's four-game window with a goal against Peru and closed it with the winner against Canada.
articles.body:
ST. PAUL, Minn. — The last day of an exhausting and enlightening U.S. camp — four friendlies over 16 days with a blend of veterans and prospects — was a cantankerous affair that looked nothing like the previous bright performances.

It was rough and sometimes violent. It lacked the rhythm and flashes of beauty that defined victories over Peru, Chile and Mexico.

Through 90 brutal minutes, however, the U.S. found another way to win, defeating Canada, 1-0, to complete a perfect return from the World Cup.

Teenager Justin Ellis fought through an injury to score in the 29th minute and goalkeeper Brian Schwake recorded a shutout in his first career start as the U.S. rebounded from a pair of losses to Canada in recent years.

Ellis, a 19-year-old striker for Orlando City, had the first and last of the 12 U.S. goals in the extended FIFA window. He had scored four minutes into his debut Sept. 26 against Peru.

The victory marked the USMNT's first four-game winning streak in FIFA windows in more than five years and the first such run in an official window that included South American or European opponents since 2016.

The U.S. will reassemble for the CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinals against Haiti, which will host the first leg Nov. 14 at a site to be announced. (The Haitians can't play at home because of security issues.) The second leg will take place Nov. 17 in Cincinnati.

With the heavy schedule, coach Mauricio Pochettino continued shuttling players in and out of the starting lineup, except for one non-stop starter: midfielder Gio Reyna, who lined up in a deeper role than previous matches. Given the amount of time he had logged, his inclusion came as a surprise. Reyna will now pivot back to his French club, Strasbourg, which will visit Nice on Sunday.

Two players made their first U.S. career starts: Schwake and 17-year-old winger Mathis Albert.

A few days ago, Pochettino hinted Schwake would get the call and become the fourth different keeper to start in this window. Schwake, 25, is in his first full season as an MLS starter, for front-running Nashville SC.

Matt Freese, the World Cup starter who got the call against Peru on Sept. 26, wasn't even in uniform Tuesday.

Albert was a sub in each of the first three games, drawing a penalty kick against Peru and, with a late goal against Chile, becoming the youngest scorer in U.S. history. (The record stood all of four days before Cavan Sullivan scored against Mexico .)

Chris Richards made his second consecutive start and wore the captain's armband, in place of Tyler Adams, who was on the bench. Richards partnered in central defense with George Campbell making his second start. Auston Trusty and Alex Freeman were in wide positions, with Freeman given the freedom to jet upfield.

Malik Tillman, who logged 192 minutes in the first three matches, started in midfield again, joined by 21-year-old Brooklyn Raines and Yunus Musah, who, at just 23, made his 50th career appearance .

Ellis made his second start at striker, replacing 18-year-old Julian Hall, who scored in each of his first three appearances.

Two of Freeman's Villarreal teammates started for Canada: forward Tani Oluwaseyi and midfielder Nathan Saliba. Atlético Madrid forward Jonathan David rounded out La Liga's contingent for Canada, which arrived after shutout victories over Peru and Chile.

Under their pugnacious American coach, Jesse Marsch, the Canadians often battered the Americans when they touched the ball. The tactic frustrated the U.S., neutralized its attack and brought protests from the U.S. bench.

Out of sorts, the Americans were sloppy and sluggish. Their giveaways allowed Canada to create threats, though none that seriously tested Schwake.

Ellis required treatment in the 21st minute after a challenge by Canadian captain Stephen Eustáquio. Despite a conspicuous limp — and multiple potential replacements warming up on the side — he returned to the match.

He was well enough to score in the 29th minute. From the right side, Freeman connected with Tillman centrally. Freeman's marker, Richie Laryea, had committed to the pass, allowing Freeman to bolt into open space and receive Tillman's return pass.

He bore down on goal before crossing into the 6-yard box, where Ellis redirected it into the net. Canadian eyes looked to the assistant referee for an offside flag. It never came. TV replays showed Ellis was barely onside or slightly beyond defender Luc de Fougerolles. Video replay is not used in friendlies; if it had been here, the goal might've been disallowed.

The bitterness continued. Reyna received a yellow card for taking down Eustáquio, who appeared to injure his shoulder. Later, after a whistle, Laryea kicked the ball at the U.S. coaches — then extended his hand to Pochettino, who playfully hugged him.

Ellis, Reyna and Musah left at halftime, replaced by Hall, Sebastian Berhalter and Sergiño Dest, respectively. Eustáquio didn't return, either.

Ellis suffered a lower right leg contusion and left the stadium before the match ended in order to get an MRI exam, a team spokesman said.

Canada set the terms but the U.S. absorbed pressure and cleared balls from danger.

Trusty absorbed a crunching blow to the head from David and required treatment.

To firm up his midfield, Pochettino inserted Adams. At the same juncture, 20-year-old winger Cole Campbell became the 13th player to debut in this camp.

Canada's pressure nearly paid off in the 64th minute, but Schwake reacted well and got a slight touch on de Fougerolles' running volley, pushing it off the crossbar.

Hall was sent in alone in the 71st minute but lacked the poise of his previous appearances and missed the near side.

The Americans continued to defend well, shielding Schwake and clearing the ball from the box.

U.S. notes : Freese and Frankie Westfield, a 20-year-old right back who debuted against Chile, were not in uniform as Pochettino remained consistent in dressing 26 players.

articles.title: From 1-1 to 1-6: India’s challenge to Uruguay ends in a harsh reality check
articles.summary: Kolkata: For a brief period on Tuesday, the Salt Lake Stadium became a cathedral of dreams for Indian football.
articles.body: Kolkata: For a brief period on Tuesday, the Salt Lake Stadium became a cathedral of dreams for Indian football.The sky was gloomy and grumpy, threatening to open up at any moment. But as the clock ticked 22 minutes, Ryan Williams, almost unnoticed, began his run from the centre line like someone feeding on his inner brute.Tottenham Hotspur midfielder Rodrigo Bentancur was left searching for answers in his wake as India’s No. 10 continued with pace and potency before unleashing a piledriver from the edge of the box. Uruguay goalkeeper Thiago Cardozo managed to parry it partially, but Anirudh Thapa followed with all his predatory instinct to snap up the rebound.Everything about the goal was so delightfully done — the thrill of it, the kill of it.Suddenly, there was life after India had conceded an 11th-minute goal through a Darwin Nunez penalty. It was 1-1 against two-time World Cup winners and a team currently ranked No. 20 in the FIFA rankings. And suddenly, Khalid Jamil’s India made their football look bold and beautiful.Then lightning struck, literally, forcing the players to leave the field. The game was suspended for a mandatory 30 minutes.When the two teams resumed the contest, Uruguay flipped the narrative with a class-topper’s swagger. Maximiliano Araujo made it 2-1 for Diego Forlan’s team going into the break.After the changeover, Forlan’s team came out with a vengeance. Araujo got his second in the 59th minute, while further goals from Rodrigo Zalazar (53), Juan Manuel Sanabria (71) and Rodrigo Sebastian Aguirre (86) completed Uruguay’s eventual 6-1 demolition of India.Amid all the fight and frustration, it was the kind of performance from Jamil’s side that was infused with a sense of hope, despite being India’s heaviest defeat at this ground, eclipsing Thailand’s 5-0 dismantling of the home side in the 1995 Nehru Cup.Through Edmund Lalrindika’s movements inside the box, Williams’ incisive run and those thunderous strikes from second-half substitutes Mohammed Sanan and Sahal Abdul Samad that forced timely interventions from the Uruguayan goalkeeper, India tried to seize their moment and showed a new way of looking the big boys in the eye.Adopting a high line against Nunez and Araujo was also a statement of intent.In such an exhibition of admirable belief, there were moments which clashed and coalesced in equal measure, but India always tried to measure up to the excessive demands of such games against World Cup regulars.It was perhaps this new India’s bold approach that forced Forlan to think differently about his game plan when play was suspended.The essence of Uruguayan football identity is rooted in ‘garra charrua’ — a dogged, street-savvy idea of rising to the challenge against all odds.After the World Cup debacle, Forlan has inherited a team which no longer thrives in this ‘garra charrua’ spirit, as reports of dressing-room mutiny and players’ defiance of his predecessor Marcelo Bielsa’s training methods marked a tense, disorderly end to the Argentine’s tenure as Uruguay coach.Whether a game against India would inspire much urgency in this respect is debatable, but it should give him an interesting window into the articles.title: ‘Thank you for making me love football even more’: Neymar’s heartfelt message to Lionel Messi after Argentina farewell
articles.summary: Neymar Jr paid an emotional tribute to Lionel Messi after the Argentina great played his final international match, describing it as an honour to have
articles.body: Neymar Jr paid an emotional tribute to Lionel Messi after the Argentina great played his final international match, describing it as an honour to have shared the pitch and made history with one of football’s greatest stars.Messi brought down the curtain on his Argentina career with a memorable performance in front of 85,000 fans at the Monumental Stadium in Buenos Aires on Tuesday, scoring a penalty and setting up two goals in a 3-0 win over Benin.The 39-year-old, who announced on August 31 that his time with Argentina was coming to an end, finished his international career with 208 appearances, 126 goals, a World Cup title and two Copa América triumphs.Neymar, who played alongside Messi at Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain, took to social media to mark the occasion.“Anyone who loves football has enjoyed you throughout all these years…Today is your final game wearing the shirt of your national team, your country, and I hope you enjoy every second of it and that all the tributes today make you happy," posted Neymar.The Brazil star said Messi's influence went far beyond Argentina and thanked his former teammate for making him appreciate football even more.“It is not only Argentina that thanks you; the whole world thanks you for everything you’ve done for football. Thank you for making me love football even more. It was an honour to have played against you, and even more so to have made history alongside you,” he signed off.Messi signs off with a gala performanceMessi ensured his farewell was worthy of the occasion. He played a role in all three goals as Argentina celebrated a 3-0 victory.Nicolás Otamendi opened the scoring in the 48th minute after connecting with a corner taken by Messi. The Argentine captain then set up Nicolás Paz for the second goal in the 61st minute before converting a left-foot penalty into the top corner 10 minutes later.The crowd repeatedly broke into chants of “Olé, olé, Messi” as the captain soaked in the occasion.The match was also briefly stopped 10 minutes after kick-off so Messi could receive a special tribute. Teammates and rivals approached him as the 85,000-strong crowd rose for a standing ovation, with Messi raising his hand in acknowledgement.He wore a special-edition Argentina jersey featuring wider vertical stripes, a giant sun and a golden No. 10 on the back. The design also carried a goat's horns, a reference to his status as the "GOAT".After the final whistle, Messi addressed the fans from the centre of the pitch.“It was a source of great pride to wear this jersey for over 20 years,” Messi told the crowd. “I never stopped fighting, never stopped giving my all. I would love to keep coming back forever, because playing for the Argentine national team is the most beautiful thing that can happen to you.”He also promised to remain close to the team even after his playing days with Argentina end.“I’m going to miss you all. Now I’ll be on your side, supporting the national team and the guys who come next,” Messi said. “When we’re united, we’re stronger than anyone and can overcome anything. Tough times lie ahead, because what this group achieved won’t be easy to repeat.”From heartbreak to World Cup gloryMessi made his Argentina debut in 2005 and endured years of disappointment with the national team before finally reaching the summit at the 2022 World Cup.The triumph in Qatar completed the major missing piece of his international career and cemented his status as a national hero, following the legacy of Diego Maradona.His journey with Argentina included two Copa América titles and six World Cup appearances. At the latest World Cup, he came close to another title, with Argentina losing 1-0 to Spain in the final. Messi still finished the tournament with eight goals and four assists.He remains the only footballer to have won the Ballon d'Or eight times and has again entered the conversation for the award.Messi's farewell was an emotional affair from the outset. Accompanied by his sons Thiago, Mateo and Ciro, he became visibly emotional during the Argentine national anthem, while goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez put an arm around him.Before taking his final victory lap, Messi left the Argentine squad with one final message.“We need to build a strong, united group because there are people who want the national team to fail, and we shouldn’t give them the satisfaction."Earlier in the day, Messi was also awarded an honorary doctorate by the University of Buenos Aires. articles.title: Samu Rodríguez: "No puedes decirle que no al Oviedo"
articles.standfirst: El futbolista repasa en MARCA sus primeros meses como azul, recuerda su primer derbi asturiano y apuesta por recuperar ante el Eibar la versión ofrecida ante al Sporting
articles.summary: El futbolista repasa en MARCA sus primeros meses como azul, recuerda su primer derbi asturiano y apuesta por recuperar ante el Eibar la versión ofrecida ante al Sporting
articles.body: Samu Rodríguez atiende a MARCA en El Requexón después del entrenamiento del Real Oviedo. El futbolista repasa sus primeros meses como azul, su adaptación a un equipo profundamente renovado y el crecimiento que está experimentando de la mano de Julián Calero. También recuerda la victoria en su primer derbi asturiano, analiza las diferencias entre el equipo dentro y fuera del Tartiere y mira ya al duelo del lunes ante el Eibar. ¿Cómo está viviendo estos primeros meses como jugador del Real Oviedo? La verdad es que muy contento. Estoy muy agradecido por la oportunidad que me han dado. Tanto la ciudad como la afición me han recibido muy bien, también los compañeros que ya llevan aquí tiempo. Estoy muy a gusto estos primeros meses y creo que va a ir a mejor. ¿Qué fue lo que más le atrajo del Oviedo cuando surgió la posibilidad de venir aquí? Al final, lo que se sabe del Oviedo: un club histórico aquí en España, que desde el primer momento mostró mucho interés por mí. Tanto Agustín como David, la gente que me llamó del club. Al final, no puedes decirle que no al Oviedo. En un equipo con tantos jugadores recién llegados y teniendo en cuenta el panorama de lesiones, ¿cómo se construye un vestuario y una identidad común en tan poco tiempo? Es positivo que haya una plantilla larga, teniendo en cuenta que estas cosas en el fútbol pasan, pero hay que estar preparado. Es una faena tener tantas lesiones. Creo que el equipo, con tantos jugadores nuevos, se está adaptando bien. Estamos cogiendo las cosas que nos pide el míster. Hay partidos buenos, partidos peores, pero creo que el equipo va dando pasos hacia adelante y vamos a ir mejorando. Ha tenido oportunidades desde que llegó. ¿Qué le pide Julián Calero cuando toca entrar en el equipo? Un poco lo que él siempre comenta en rueda de prensa. Nos pide que seamos un equipo sólido, que lo estamos siendo. Quitando este último partido de Elda y el de Sabadell, estamos concediendo muy poco atrás y yo creo que estoy mejorando mucho defensivamente. Estamos dando esos números positivos y luego, en ataque, que tenga personalidad y que juegue como yo soy. ¿En qué aspectos cree que has evolucionado más desde que llegó y en cuáles cree que todavía tiene margen de mejora? Soy un jugador muy joven todavía. Tengo muchísimo margen de mejora. Creo que el míster me está ayudando mucho en la faceta defensiva, estoy dando un paso adelante. Me ha tocado defender a jugadores complicados de la categoría, como David González o Guille Rosas, que son jugadores muy buenos. Creo que estoy dando un gran nivel defensivo, que al final es lo que me pide el míster. Coger esa experiencia en la categoría e ir soltándome como lo que soy yo. Seguro que voy a ir subiendo el nivel. Ha tenido la oportunidad de vivir un derbi y, además, ganarlo en el Tartiere. ¿Cómo vivió aquel partido? Increíble. Desde que nos levantamos ese día, se veía por las calles a todo el mundo con la camiseta del equipo. El recibimiento fue una locura desde dentro del bus. Luego, saltar al campo y ver el estadio repleto, lo que la gente alentó... Nos ayudaron un montón. ¿Qué valoración hace de la victoria ante el Sporting? Creo que fue el mejor partido del equipo. Fue un partido súper completo en el que no concedimos apenas. Fuimos un equipo valiente, fue merecido. Me alegro mucho, tanto por el equipo como por la afición. El Carlos Tartiere y la afición generan una exigencia importante. ¿Cómo vive esa presión y qué sensaciones tiene cuando juega en casa? Más que presión, la verdad es que ayuda un montón porque la gente te da su ánimo. Desde mi llegada, me han recibido con los brazos abiertos y para nada es presión. Impresiona entrar en un estadio y que haya 30.000 personas todos los fines de semana, pero la afición del Oviedo es lo que ya se conoce. Con su equipo a muerte y, en vez de presión, lo que nos da es ánimo. En casa se ha visto una buena versión del equipo y fuera ha habido un poco más de todo. ¿Qué cree que cambia en ese contraste? Fuera de casa vas al estadio donde la gente aprieta. El equipo que juega en casa siempre intenta ser más protagonista y te aprieta más. Pero creo que tuvimos un gran inicio fuera de casa. Ganamos en Albacete y en Valladolid, además concediendo poco, portería a cero los dos días. En Sabadell fue un contexto diferente, no entramos bien al partido. Y el otro día en Elda nos condenaron un poco errores individuales. Pero estábamos concediendo muy poco, siendo un equipo muy sólido, que se estaba reflejando en los números, y creo que hay que seguir por ese camino. En casa, como el último día ante el Sporting, estábamos dando una grandísima versión, pero no estaban entrando los goles. Atrás estábamos siendo muy sólidos y hay que continuar como el partido del Sporting. Viene el líder, el Eibar, en una categoría tremendamente igualada. ¿Cómo ve el partido? Tenemos una semana larga para preparar el partido. Viene el Eibar, que lleva siete victorias consecutivas, pero no le tenemos miedo a nadie y sabemos que en casa somos muy fuertes. El lunes vamos a tener 20.000 personas apoyándonos y, con mucha valentía, a recuperar esas sensaciones del día del Sporting y a ganar el partido.

No es del todo así, pero se entiende... Toca, en fin, revisar la clasificación ahora, para ver dónde andaba cada uno a mediados de septiembre, que fue cuando se paró la cosa. Para cuando haya que escribir otra columna de éstas, show must go on, habrá regresado hasta la Champions. articles.title: "Cinco mil millones de razones para el veredicto"
articles.standfirst: Directivos de la Premier esperan sanción dura contra el City y que no caigan los derechos de TV e interés en su Liga. División entre los equipos sobre qué prefieren
articles.summary: Directivos de la Premier esperan sanción dura contra el City y que no caigan los derechos de TV e interés en su Liga. División entre los equipos sobre qué prefieren
articles.body: Directivos de la Premier League temen que la integridad de la competición y los derechos de retransmisión multimillonarios se vean dañados irreversiblemente si el Manchester City evita un castigo severo tras ser declarado culpable de engordar artificialmente sus cuentas casi una década. Según un importante directivo del fútbol, en referencia al valor del actual contrato televisivo, "había cinco mil millones de razones para el veredicto" de la semana pasada. Eximirles de culpa por esos "contratos fraudulentos" pone en peligro a toda la liga. Así lo explica el prestigioso diario 'The Telegraph' tras sondear a altos ejecutivos. Un experto legal consultado incluso argumentó que si se aplicaran las mismas directrices de sanción que en los casos contra el Nottingham Forest y el Everton (deducción de puntos por cada 5 millones de trampa en el gasto), el City podría perder entre 160 y 200 puntos, que deberían distribuirse a lo largo de varias temporadas, dado que no se pueden obtener todos los puntos en una sola campaña. Sin embargo, los clubes están divididos, incluso los de Segunda, por lo que una demanda colectiva, uniendo fuerzas contra el City, se considera improbable. Para presionar claro, porque hay que recordar que en la sanción final no tendrán voz ni voto. Algunos quieren la sanción más severa, pero otros temen que la expulsión también mengue el poder de la Premier, su interés en general más allá de los derechos de TV, e incluso logre revivir una Superliga. Los jugadores siguen charlando con sus abogados buscando posibles compensaciones a bonus no ganados por posiciones no obtenidas, por lucro cesante. Abu Dhabi amenaza incluso con menguar sus inversiones en Inglaterra si hay sanción, y el primer ministro británico navega entre dos aguas en sus declaraciones. El City presumiblemente perdería el apoyo del país (por no hablar de los otros 11 equipos relacionados con Grupo City), pérdida de jugadores, no poder pagar el restante que le queda de varios fichajes (con daño por tanto a otros equipos incluso europeos), el descrédito, multas, nuevos dueños... Un lío que se puede prolongar en el tiempo porque si el City recurriera una posible sanción al Tribunal Supremo (no puede al TAS, al circunscribirse este caso a Gran Bretaña), cuyos jueces ya no son expertos en deporte, la cosa podría dar un vuelco. Por no hablar de que si el City quedase libre de cargos... el costo del caso por valor de unos 100 millones correría a cargo de los clubes. El equipo apeló el pasado viernes 2 de octubre y ahora se abren 12 semanas para analizar las apelaciones, y Comité independiente tendrá otros 30 días adicionales para emitir su veredicto, que debería estar listo entre finales de diciembre y enero. Aunque vista la profundidad del caso, a nadie le extrañaría que se alargara algo más.

articles.title: Raúl Varela proclama a Messi como "el más grande" tras su despedida: "El nuevo Rey Mago de nuestras vidas"
articles.standfirst: El presentador de La Tribu contrapone la despedida del argentino con el momento que vive Cristiano Ronaldo con Portugal
articles.summary: El presentador de La Tribu contrapone la despedida del argentino con el momento que vive Cristiano Ronaldo con Portugal
articles.body: La despedida de Leo Messi como internacional argentino y la situación que atraviesa Cristiano Ronaldo con Portugal dejaron dos imágenes muy diferentes que Raúl Varela quiso contraponer en La Tribu. El periodista terminó rendido a la figura del argentino después de volver a verle liderar a la Albiceleste. Mientras España remontaba en Croacia, Cristiano Ronaldo hacía pública una carta tras lo sucedido con Portugal. "Cristiano Ronaldo decidía escribir una carta donde no acaba de quedar muy claro si pide perdón o pide que le pidan perdón", arrancó Varela. El director de La Tribu resumió así el mensaje del portugués: "Que sí, que se merece el tirón de orejas, pero que le han hecho calentar en la banda más tiempo del debido. Que Portugal es lo más importante, pero su capital no es Lisboa sino CR7". Varela contrapuso ese momento con el homenaje recibido por Messi: "Ese momento epistolar del segundo mejor jugador de los tiempos modernos coincidió en tiempo pero no en forma con la carta que toda Argentina y en cierto modo todo el mundo le escribió a Leo Messi en su partido de despedida como internacional argentino". El periodista recordó toda la trayectoria del argentino con su selección: "Un título mundial, otra final perdida, algún momento difícilmente explicable por lo ingrato que le tocó vivir, pero toda la magia del planeta Tierra para este cuarto Rey Mago al que el propio Cristiano Ronaldo le acabará escribiendo de alguna manera". La figura de Messi, además, trascendió al propio partido. "Ayer en todas las zonas mixtas del mundo se preguntó por Messi", destacó Varela. Para Varela, lo visto en esta última etapa termina decantando definitivamente su valoración: "Aún le quedan cuatro bailes mal contados en Miami, pero después de verle ayer liderar otra vez a la albiceleste de Scaloni, de hacer el torneo que hizo en Estados Unidos, de promover la fantasía de su candidatura al Balón de Oro que sigue sin dueño y el contraste con la forma de despedirse de su alter ego portugués no queda más que proclamarlo como el más grande". Y cerró su reflexión con una comparación especialmente gráfica: "Es esa ciudad de Roma donde todos los caminos conducen a él. A Leo Messi. Después de Melchor, Gaspar y Baltasar, el nuevo rey mago de nuestras vidas".

articles.title: La junta militar que desafía a la FIFA: "Nuestro fútbol está enfermo y vamos a encontrar los remedios"
articles.standfirst: Ibrahim Traoré, jefe de la junta militar de Burkina Faso, anunció medidas inminentes en el fútbol burkinés incluso a riesgo de desafiar a la FIFA
articles.summary: Ibrahim Traoré, jefe de la junta militar de Burkina Faso, anunció medidas inminentes en el fútbol burkinés incluso a riesgo de desafiar a la FIFA
articles.body: Ibrahim Traoré, el jefe de la junta militar de Burkina Faso tras liderar un golpe de Estado el 30 de septiembre de 2022, ha prometido una reforma del fútbol burkinés tras la dura goleada que sufrió su selección por 7-0 contra Argentina. El viaje a Buenos Aires se convirtió en un quebradero de cabeza, hasta el punto de obligar a Burkina Faso a recurrir de urgencia a la selección sub-23 y a llegar a Argentina apenas unas horas antes del inicio del partido. "Nuestro fútbol está enfermo y vamos a encontrar los remedios. Porque para reinvertir, primero hay que curar la dolencia", declaró el joven militar al recibir a la selección femenina sub-15, que fue subcampeona del campeonato escolar africano. Ibrahim Traoré (14 de marzo de 1988) anunció medidas inminentes, incluso a riesgo de desafiar a la FIFA, para intentar poner orden en el fútbol nacional. "No tenemos elección, estamos obligados a intervenir a fondo, nos suspendan o no", afirmó. El "nos suspendan o no" es una frase cargada de posibles consecuencias por parte de la FIFA, que según sus estatutos cada federación miembro debe gestionar sus asuntos de manera independiente y sin injerencias indebidas de gobiernos o terceros. Un intervención directa del Estado en los nombramientos o en el funcionamiento de la Federación de Burkina Faso podría exponer al país a sanciones que llegarían incluso a la suspensión.

articles.title: Chile frena el despegue de la era Márquez
articles.standfirst: Maximiliano Gutiérrez y Vicente Pizarro hicieron los goles
articles.summary: Maximiliano Gutiérrez y Vicente Pizarro hicieron los goles
articles.body: Los goles de Maximiliano Gutiérrez y Vicente Pizarro frenaron este martes el despegue de la era Rafa Márquez al frente de la selección mexicana en un duelo amistoso contra Chile, en el que el Tri cayó por 0-2 y dejó al descubierto las carencias de un equipo en transición para garantizar resultados. Un remate de Gutiérrez desde el centro del área hacia el centro de la portería, asistido por Gonzalo Tapia tras un rápido contraataque, adelantó a los chilenos en el marcador en el minuto 56 ante la pasividad de la zaga azteca. Justo cuando México reestructuraba su once con los cambios y sin tiempo para asimilarlos, Pizarro firmó un zurdazo al ángulo inferior izquierdo que sentenció el encuentro en favor de los chilenos en el minuto 65. En el cuarto partido de Rafa Márquez como seleccionador mexicano, disputado en el emblemático Estadio Memorial Coliseo de Los Ángeles, su equipo buscaba resarcirse del amargo comienzo tras la derrota de la semana pasada ante Estados Unidos (3-0) y los empates contra Colombia (1-1) y Perú (1-1). Este balance en el inicio del nuevo técnico tras la salida de Javier Aguirre evidencia un proceso de transición condicionado por la falta de victorias y propone como reto consolidar un bloque competitivo que asegure resultados.

articles.title: Barcelona passed up two chances to sign Atletico Madrid superstar for just €5 million
articles.summary: Barcelona had the chance to sign Marc Pubill for just €5 million in 2023, but opted for the experience of Joao Cancelo instead. Two years later, the decision...
articles.body:
Barcelona had the chance to sign Marc Pubill for just €5 million in 2023, but opted for the experience of Joao Cancelo instead.

Two years later, the decision looks increasingly significant as the former Levante full-back has developed into an established Atletico Madrid and Spain player.

According to SPORT , Pubill was already on Barcelona's radar when he was 20 and playing for Levante.

The club's sporting department liked his profile, but former manager Xavi Hernandez's side wanted a more experienced solution at right-back and waited for Cancelo to become available from Manchester City.

Pubill subsequently joined Almeria for the same €5m fee and has since seen his market value rise considerably.

Pubill was available for only €5 million

Barcelona's opportunity came at a time when Levante needed to generate income.

Barcelona passed on the opportunity to sign Pubill twice. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images)

Pubill had impressed as a young right-back and was already representing Spain at Under-21 level, making him an attractive long-term option.

However, Barça chose patience over committing to the youngster. Cancelo eventually forced through a loan move from Manchester City and arrived in the final hours of the 2023 summer transfer window.

That decision changed Pubill's career path. He moved to Almeria for €5m, with Levante also retaining 20 per cent of a future capital gain.

The full-back then spent two seasons developing there before attracting considerably greater interest.

Pubill nearly joined Barcelona again in 2024

Notably, Barcelona had another opportunity a year later.

When Pubill's proposed €16m move to Atalanta collapsed, Barça explored a different route.

Marc Pubill could have played for Barcelona. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images)

The club attempted to bring him in on a paid loan with an option to buy, an arrangement that could have generated around €12m for Almeria across two seasons.

The deal ultimately failed to materialise, while Pubill remained at Almeria for another campaign in the second division. Notably, the player had given his approval to joining Barcelona, but it did not happen.

Barcelona missed out as Atletico Madrid secure Pubill

Barcelona eventually stepped away from the race, with Jules Kounde established at right-back and other areas taking priority.

Atletico Madrid moved decisively in 2025, signing Pubill for €12m plus €7m in potential variables, and his subsequent development has only increased the significance of Barcelona's earlier decision.

Fast forward, his valuation has risen to €50m (Transfermarkt), while Pubill has become an important player for Diego Simeone and a regular with Spain.

articles.title: Republic of Ireland women: 'Nothing can take my attention away' - Carla Ward on World Cup
articles.summary: Republic of Ireland manager Carla Ward says that "nothing is tempting" her away from her job as they prepare for a World Cup qualifying double-header against Kazakhstan.
articles.body:
Republic of Ireland manager Carla Ward says that her focus is on reaching the Women's World Cup amid speculation linking her to a move back to the Women's Super League.

The Republic have a chance to book a spot at next summer's finals in Brazil when they face a play-off against Kazakhstan before, if they progress, a two-legged final against either Belgium or Poland.

Ward, who replaced Eileen Gleeson in January 2025, has been linked with the vacant post at her former club Aston Villa. However, she insists leading the Republic of Ireland to the World Cup is her primary ambition.

"Nothing is tempting when I'm in this job, you know I love this job and I love working here," Ward said.

"I don't think anything can take my attention away from these next four games so it's not a conversation and it's not anything I would entertain.

"My heart and my focus, I came here to try and get to a World Cup and that's all I'm going to think about for the next four games."

'The message is very clear, no complacency'

The Republic of Ireland made history when they qualified for the World Cup in 2023 for the first time ever. However, they were unable to progress from the group, beaten by co-hosts Australia and Canada, before drawing with Nigeria.

Three years on, Ward now has the chance to lead the team back to the biggest stage in international football.

"You've seen how I've spoken in the last two years and with immense pride in this job," she continued.

"I'm here because I want to get to a World Cup and I think we've made tremendous strides and steps as a nation, and it would be the cherry on the cake, but, look we've got four games, four cup finals.

"We have to give everything, blood, sweat and tears. We have to leave everything out there in everything we do and if we do that, we've got every chance."

The two-legged tie against Kazakhstan begins with a trip to the Astana Arena on Friday, 9 October (12:00 BST) before the return fixture in Cork four days later.

The Republic of Ireland are unbeaten at Pairc Ui Chaoimh, but Ward is taking nothing for granted against a Kazakhstan side ranked 98th in the world.

"We have to go up another level, we have to make sure that we're performing, and we're focused at the highest level.

"If we do that then we'll get the job done. We've got an unbelievable squad that are hugely talented and they will look after each other.

"I think anyone that comes in that will know their role I think we're really clear with what we do, what we want and how we play."

'I have full belief in every single one of this group'

Ward will have to make changes, with captain Katie McCabe and Marissa Sheva both suspended for the first leg, while the experienced Denise O'Sullivan is also unavailable.

Tara O'Hanlon is out with a hamstring injury and Saoirse Noonan has also been ruled out of both games with an ankle problem.

Meanwhile, Crystal Palace midfielder Shanade Hopcroft has been called into the squad for the first time.

Despite the absence of multiple key leaders, Ward says this is a chance for others to shine.

"No matter who plays, naturally when you take the likes of Katie and Denise out of your team, they're two big leaders but that's an opportunity for players to step up.

"Katie's here for a reason, she's got a big part to play off the pitch, and she will and she'll lead the group as she normally does.

"Then it'll be over to those that go out there and I have full belief in every single one of this group to go and get the job done."

articles.title: Livakovic aplaude su regreso al Barça
articles.standfirst: Ha encajado 14 goles en los cuatro partidos con Croacia
articles.summary: Ha encajado 14 goles en los cuatro partidos con Croacia
articles.body: Dominik Livakovic es el portero titular de la selección de Croacia. Es un fijo en su combinado nacional, y ha salido de inicio, y completado, los cuatro encuentros del equipo balcánico de estas últimas semanas. Pero no han sido partidos, en dos se ha medido a España, plácidos. El veterano arquero ha encajado ¡14! goles. En las próximas horas, se sumará al Barça, donde su trayectoria está siendo más plácida y donde tiene opciones de salir de inicio este próximo sábado si Joan García sigue sin recuperarse de sus molestias, aunque el catalán se entrenó hoy con el grupo y parece que regresará al once. Livakovic, de 31 años, es uno de los 17 internacionales que el Barcelona ha tenido repartidos con sus respectivas selecciones estas últimas semanas. Ha sido titular en los cuatro cruces de Croacia, todos correspondientes a la fase de grupos de la Nations League. Pero no han sido compromisos fáciles para el arquero culé: su balance fue de una victoria, contra Chequia (2-1) y tres derrotas: perdió contra la Inglaterra de Anthony Gordon (7-0) y frente a la España de Lamine, Pedri, Fermín, Rodri... en los dos cruces contra los de Luis de la Fuente. Cayó contra la Roja por 4-1 y 2-1. El exguardameta del Dinamo de Zagreb, además, sufrió en estos compromisos con Croacia a sus compañeros del Barça: Lamine le marcó dos tantos en el primer cruce y Anthony Gordon también fue protagonista en la histórica goleada de Inglaterra: el bloque de Tuchel se impuso por 7-0. Pero en las próximas horas regresa a la disciplina culé. Está previsto que se incorpore mañana, junto a los internacionales españoles. Y en el equipo catalán sus jornadas y partidos se presumen mucho más plácidos: el Barça lidera la tabla de Primera en solitario, ha ganado todos los encuentros, y es de los menos goleados: ha encajado siete dianas en los siete primeros choques de LaLiga. Livakovic, fichado este verano y con contrato hasta 2030, fue titular contra el Sevilla en el Pizjuán, donde debutó como culé, y todo apunta a que se mantendrá bajo palos, en el cruce contra el Getafe de este sábado en el Spotify Camp Nou, si Joan García sigue de baja por sus molestias en la rodilla, aunque el catalán se entrenó hoy con el grupo y parece que volverá.

articles.title: Football: South Korea to review military exemption after Asian Games row
articles.summary: South Korea are discussing making changes to military exemptions for athletes after Asian Games controversy.
articles.body:
South Korea's government says it intends to review the military exemptions it grants athletes after the controversy surrounding South Korean footballers at the Asian Games.

Following their win against hosts Japan in the final, three players were criticised for celebrating securing their exemptions, including South Korea captain Lee Gi-hyuk.

South Korean men are required to undertake between 18 and 21 months of active military service before the age of 28.

Lee apologised for his remarks , but Culture, Sports and Tourism minister Choi Hwi-young says he will "review" the exemption.

Choi called Lee's comments "utterly immature" and said the system, which has been in place for more than 50 years, "will inevitably have to be scaled back".

South Korean captain Lee sparked outrage in his home country when he held up his gold medal and triumphantly announced he was "not going to the military".

The government rewards Asian Games champions and Olympic medal winners of any colour with a service exemption bar basic training, which lasts less than a month.

"It is true that the system has contributed to helping outstanding artists and athletes maintain and develop their abilities," Choi said at a National Assembly Culture, Sports and Tourism Committee hearing.

Captain apologises for gloating over military service exemption

'Grateful, proud and at peace' - emotional Messi plays final Argentina game

"However, the values attached to fairness and public perceptions of military service have changed. I agree that the system should be comprehensively reviewed once again."

Cho Kye-won, a member of the Democratic Party of Korea, questioned Choi on the topic and said the incident "left young people with a serious sense of unfairness".

The current system grants exemptions only to Olympic medallists finishing third or better and to Asian Games gold medallists, and more than 80% of those benefits are concentrated in the Asian Games.

He suggested winning a world championship in any sport is harder than winning the Asian Games, yet world champions in other sports receive no service benefit.

"Of the 44 people who qualified for the benefit at this Asian Games, 36 were in soccer and baseball," Cho said.

articles.title: El Celta es el equipo de LaLiga que menos encaja como visitante
articles.standfirst: Sólo un gol y no ha perdido fuera de Balaídos en la competición doméstica
articles.summary: Sólo un gol y no ha perdido fuera de Balaídos en la competición doméstica
articles.body: El Celta es el equipo de LaLiga que menos goles recibe como visitante, únicamente ha encajado un tanto. Fue en Getafe y el autor fue Martín Satriano. En los otros dos desplazamientos, ante el Valencia y Real Sociedad, los encuentros concluyeron sin goles. Los de Claudio Giráldez intentarán el próximo domingo, en Elche, seguir sumando fuera de Balaídos. Esta temporada no saben lo que es perder en LaLiga fuera de Vigo, sumando tres empates en igual número de desplazamientos. El Celta necesita sumar puntos para mejorar su situación clasificatoria de arranque de temporada, a pesar de irse al parón goleando al Racing de Santander con un 5-0. Para ello nada mejor que hacerlo como visitante, si nos atenemos a los número de la pasada temporada y los de la presente. Los célticos suman prácticamente los mismos números en Balaídos que fuera de casa. Apenas uno más como locales y con un partido más disputado. Esto prolonga la tendencia de la pasada temporada en la que los célticos ya fueron de los mejores visitante del campeonato, sumando 31 puntos fuera de Vigo y que supuso firmar su mejor campaña como foráneos en toda su historia en Primera división. Fueron ocho puntos más que los conseguidos en Balaídos.

articles.title: Scotland: What did we learn from Sebastian Pocognoli's first four Nations League games in charge?
articles.summary: The Belgian guided Scotland to one win from his first four games as head coach; they sit third in Nations League group B1; they are at home to North Macedonia on November 13 with a trip to Switzerland three days later
articles.body:
Behind the scenes, they got revolution. On the pitch, evolution, in flashes.

Sebastien Pocognoli's football is - in essence - what he promised it to be. Front-foot, attacking and aggressive.

However, perhaps not in the same way that everyone assumed when a fresh faced 39-year-old walked through the doors of Hampden Park as the Tartan Army's symbol of the modern progressive game.

In his first camp as Scotland boss, we were privy to the good (North Macedonia away), the bad (Switzerland at home), and the ugly (Slovenia at home).

Slovenia away was somehow all of the above in one game.

Aside from the convoluted, yet potentially damaging, implications for seeding for Euro 2028 qualification, here are three things we have learned from Pocognoli's first four matches in charge.

The formation which served predecessor Clarke so well in the early days of his Scotland tenure was Pocognoli's preferred shape at Monaco and Union Saint-Gilloise - so this comes as no real surprise.

The contention lies not in its deployment, but its functionality.

On paper, it makes sense. The squad has been starved of wingers and feasted on full-backs for almost a decade.

However, with 20-year-old rising star Ben Gannon-Doak as well as Josh McPake and Findlay Curtis all included in the squad, the question was where would Scotland's creative wide players all fit in.

Gannon-Doak started both of Scotland's final two matches at wing-back with captain, and now centurion, Andy Robertson operating on the opposite flank.

With a natural winger on one side and a full-back on the other, the asymmetry of the new shape should, in theory, make Scotland more elastic. Yet a lack of deep runners made them look more rigid.

When the Scotland boss flipped to a back four in the closing stages of Tuesday's dismal defeat to Slovenia, Curtis and McPake immediately looked more threatening than the players they replaced as out-and-out wingers.

The only distinct tinkering in Pocognoli's starting system came in attack.

The new head coach used a 3-5-2 in his first three matches - with McGinn in behind two No 9s - before switching to a 3-4-2-1 against Slovenia as McGinn and Ryan Christie provided support for Oli McBurnie as two No 10s.

While McBurnie, Kieron Bowie and Robbie Ure all impressed at different points throughout the camp, there may only be room for one to start in Scotland's strongest team going forward.

Talisman John McGinn - whose penalty against North Macedonia moved him level with Lawrie Reilly as the country's fourth-highest scorer of all time - will surely partner returning hero Scott McTominay in that area next month once the Napoli star fully recovers from minor heart surgery.

McTominay and McGinn have been a dangerous double act for the best part of a decade now, so they almost have to start. But will that change be made to suit personnel or suit the team?

Central to the Pocognoli press is reimagined Napoli midfielder Billy Gilmour.

The 25-year-old - who earned his 50th cap on Tuesday - has transitioned from quarterback to seeker.

Primarily a deep-lying playmaker with outstanding press-beating qualities, the former Chelsea man was deployed in a more advanced role by his new international manager to use his energy to smother opponents and his exceptional technical prowess to try to unpick blocks instead of breaking lines.

But like all tactical decisions, it's a gamble.

Gilmour's advanced starting position quite often left Scotland vulnerable to counter-attacks, and the lack of pace in Scotland's back three was exposed in those transition moments. He is also still expected to be the team's most important component in the build-up, thus expending a lot energy at both ends of the pitch.

That being said, most Scotland fans would probably still highlight him as their best player from this camp.

Whether he is eventually preferred at six, eight or 10, Gilmour is clearly going to be a key player for the new head coach.

articles.title: El Sevilla arranca la preparación para visitar al Levante con la vuelta de tres internacionales
articles.standfirst: Los hispalenses recuperan a Vlachodimos, Sangante y Kochorashvili, mientras Stassin sigue apurando sus opciones
articles.summary: Los hispalenses recuperan a Vlachodimos, Sangante y Kochorashvili, mientras Stassin sigue apurando sus opciones
articles.body: Este miércoles, el Sevilla ha retomado el trabajo en la ciudad deportiva después de tres días de descanso con una sesión más extensa de lo habitual. De esta forma, el conjunto hispalense arranca su semana de preparación con vistas a la reanudación del campeonato de Liga, que lo llevará a visitar al Levante en el Ciutat de València el próximo lunes 12 de octubre (21:00 horas). La gran novedad en esta jornada matutina ha sido el retorno de tres de los seis futbolistas que han viajado con sus respectivas selecciones nacionales. Además de Fran González, que ya volvió la pasada semana e incluso pudo disputar el Trofeo Antonio Puerta, se han unido al resto del grupo Odysseas Vlachodimos, Arouna Sangante y Giorgi Kochorashvili. Todavía quedan por reincorporarse a la plantilla sevillista tanto Gabriel Suazo como Robbie Ure. El capitán chileno participó 92 minutos en el amistoso frente a México celebrado anoche en el Memorial Coliseum de Los Ángeles, donde los sudamericanos se llevaron el triunfo por 0-2; en el caso del escocés, saltó al césped en el minuto 87 en la derrota ante Eslovenia en Hampden Park por 1-2, correspondiente a la división B de la Liga de Naciones. En cuanto a las ausencias, Luis García Plaza continúa sin poder disponer de Marcao y Lucas Stassin por lesión. El brasileño y el belga se marcharon al gimnasio tras la charla inicial junto con el defensa del filial Iker Muñoz, que lleva varias semanas con problemas físicos. Por parte del delantero, el cuerpo técnico mantiene la esperanza de que llegue a tiempo para viajar a Valencia. Otra de las buenas noticias corre de nuevo a cargo de Kike Salas y Rubén Vargas. Ambos han aprovechado el parón internacional para su puesta a punto y continúan ejercitándose con total normalidad, por lo que previsiblemente podrían reaparecer con el equipo en el encuentro ante el Levante.

articles.title: 'Looking for a screen, even if we have to stand': Benin fans savour being Lionel Messi’s last opponents
articles.summary: For football fans in Benin, Tuesday’s match against Argentina was less about the result and more about witnessing Lionel Messi’s final international
articles.body: For football fans in Benin, Tuesday’s match against Argentina was less about the result and more about witnessing Lionel Messi’s final international appearance.Benin lost 3-0 in Buenos Aires in front of more than 80,000 spectators, but the score was almost an afterthought on a night when one of the world’s greatest players said goodbye to international football.In Cotonou, screens were set up in restaurants and bars across different neighbourhoods so fans could watch the historic occasion. The match kicked off at midnight local time in Benin, but that did not stop supporters from searching for a place to watch."We're looking for a screen, even if we have to stand," said one young worker, as quoted by news agency AFP.A few "Go Benin" chants could be heard during the national anthems, but the fans watching in Benin were mostly focused on 39-year-old Messi, knowing they were watching a special moment in world football."It's an honour that Benin is the last team Messi faces," said Sylvestre Dagbedji, 34, a security guard and self-declared Messi fan."We'll always remember that it was against Benin that he retired from international football," he added.Sitting nearby, Armand Folly, 27, a motorcycle taxi driver, said: "It's going to be tough for us Beninese. Messi is a great player. I'm so proud of him for his career."During the match, supporters cheered the Cheetahs whenever they tried to break through Argentina's defence. But the biggest cheers were reserved for Messi, with fans applauding every time the former Barcelona forward and eight-time Ballon d'Or winner received the ball."I'm sad because Messi won't play anymore. He was excellent at Barca, I don't know who will be able to play like him again," said Toussain Kpadonou, a craftsman, who was watching with around a hundred people in front of a giant screen.Younger fans were also happy to watch the final international appearance of a player who has been part of the football world for two decades."Messi is a god of football, the best player in the world. He performed so well throughout his entire career, from Barca to Inter Miami," said Destin Avere, 17, as quoted by AFP.In the 71st minute, Messi stepped up to take a penalty after already providing two assists. When he found the back of the net, the crowd in Benin erupted.By then, Benin's defeat had already been forgotten. articles.title: B/R Men's International Team Power Rankings After September and October 2026 Fixtures
articles.summary: The September-October international break has finally drawn to a close after what seemed like an eternity.
articles.body:
The September-October international break has finally drawn to a close after what seemed like an eternity.

The 2026 World Cup set a bar for excitement that was unfortunately impossible for teams to reach, with friendly matches, tournament qualifiers, and Nations League games having significantly reduced stakes for all involved.

However, there were still plenty of conclusions to be drawn from those meetings, with the retirements of star players and the arrival of new managers changing the landscape for national teams as they prepare for the next major tournament.

With that in mind, we've ranked the top 10 footballing nations following the early-fall slate of games, formulating the order by judging the latest results, player performances, and quality of opponents.

Think you can do better? Leave your rankings in the comments.

Mexico was the most competitive of the host nations at the 2026 World Cup, which gives them a fair amount of credit in the bank. El Tri were extremely unlucky to lose to England in the Round of 16 after pushing the Three Lions to the limit.

The wheels have come off slightly, though, with two defeats and two draws in the September-October international break.

With that in mind, perhaps 10th seems generous. But with one of those draws coming against Colombia, and not many surrounding teams doing enough to push Mexico further down the rankings, they get a pass.

However, new manager Rafa Marquez needs to get a grip on things soon to avoid truly losing the momentum the national team gained from a memorable World Cup performance.

Colombia perhaps should have done better at the 2026 World Cup, with Switzerland there for the taking in the round of 16. Exiting the competition on penalties is always painful, but they were not beaten over 90 minutes during the summer tournament, so a lot of heart can be taken from that.

It wasn't a great international break for Los Cafeteros , who could only draw with Mexico before succumbing to a 1-0 defeat to a battling Paraguayan side. However, a 2-0 victory over Peru will instill some confidence, if not fully banish the hurt of missing out on the World Cup quarterfinals. The absence of star player Luis Diaz from the squad is also a factor in those disappointing results.

With Brazil out of sorts and Argentina adjusting to life without Lionel Messi, a solid run of performances over the coming months leading up to the 2028 Copa America would make Colombia a heavy favorite to win the competition, marking a first national title since 2001.

While the Netherlands sit happily at the top of Nations League Group A2, that's only on the basis of goals scored.

The Oranje 's eight points are level with Greece, and Germany sits only three points behind in third. Back-to-back wins against Serbia were to be expected from a team with so much star quality, and draws against the other group members were perhaps to be expected as well.

So, the Netherlands are solid but not spectacular as it stands, which is just fine as the players get used to life under new head coach Xavi. There is still the feeling, though, that the Oranje should be more competitive than they are.

A round-of-16 World Cup exit was truly disappointing for Brazil, with Carlo Ancelotti unable to get the best out of the talent at his disposal.

However, it was still one stage better than the Netherlands, which justifies the Seleçao Canarinho's place above the Oranje in the power rankings.

A 1-1 draw with Australia on September 25 suggested Don Carlo was still figuring things out, but things quickly improved. A rematch saw his side run away with a 4-2 victory, while a meeting with India brought another four goals, this time with none conceded. Still, the latter is ranked 138th by FIFA, so there's only so much you can read into that result.

The jury remains out on this Brazil side. With Copa America nearly two years away, there is plenty of time for Ancelotti to settle on his best XI and fully implement his playing style in the squad. It would be great to see some evidence of coherence sooner rather than later, though.

Morocco has a problem in the power ranking stakes. While the Atlas Lions habitually prove competitive on the world stage, they struggle to climb higher in this list because their opponents are often not of the highest standard when they head off for international camps.

This time around, they took on Gabon (85th in FIFA's ranking), Lesotho (150th), and Mali (47th), with only the first two games coming in a truly competitive setting—Africa Cup of Nations qualification matches. A 1-1 draw with Mali in a friendly also doesn't do much to bump them up the power ranking chart, either.

Still, when it comes to proper tournaments, you just know Morocco will be tough to beat. For now, though, the nation peaks at sixth.

Portugal's international break got off to an awkward start. Cristiano Ronaldo was ineffective against Wales, leading new manager Jorge Jesus to drop the football legend to the bench for the match against Norway.

After being an unused substitute in that game, the 41-year-old left the team's camp. Arguably, his absence worked to the Seleção's advantage.

Portugal ended up securing four wins from four, landing atop Nations League Group A4 with a six-point cushion.

Whether this signals the end of Ronaldo's international career remains to be seen, but Jesus has shown he is willing to leave him out of the starting XI, despite his career achievements.

This could be a start of a new era for the Portugal national team, which has been long overdue.

After a feisty World Cup, including a fiery aftermath to an unsuccessful final, Argentina hasn't done much to win over followers of international football.

The love is even harder to find now that Lionel Messi, the nation's hero and perhaps the greatest footballer ever, has officially retired from international duty after a 3-0 win against Benin, in which he scored from the penalty spot and made two assists.

Because of that seismic change for La Albiceleste, they tumble a few spots in our ranking relative to the nation's placement in FIFA's official list.

Three wins from three in the September-October break look impressive, coming with a combined scoreline of 14-0. But with those three opponents—Bolivia, Burkina Faso and Benin—all ranked around 76th by FIFA, that looks far less convincing.

Looking at England's results and performances from this international break, the World Cup increasingly seems like a missed opportunity.

However, a 3-2 loss to Spain suggests they may still have been toppled in the final if they hadn't thrown it all away against Argentina.

Head coach Thomas Tuchel has apparently discovered how to get the best out of Jude Bellingham, and Harry Kane remains unplayable. Meanwhile, Anthony Gordon has emerged as a preferred option on the left flank, notching three goals in the three games he featured in.

England will be considered among the favorites heading into Euro 2028, but there's still plenty of time between now and the tournament for customary doubts to creep in.

France has an absolute embarrassment of riches to choose from. Being able to call upon Kylian Mbappé, Ousmane Dembélé, Désiré Doué, Rayan Cherki, Michael Olise, and Bradley Barcola in attack is frankly outrageous.

It was three wins and a draw from four matches in the September-October international break, with the new boss taking little time to settle into the role. Les Bleus are sitting pretty at the top of Nations League Group A1, and it will be fascinating to see how they progress in the coming months.

For now, Zidane will be thrilled with what he's seen, although a more clinical edge needs to be applied to the aesthetically pleasing football. The players have been let off the leash a bit to create chances and bamboozle opposing defenses, but just one goal each against Turkiye, Belgium, and Italy in the first three matches was certainly disappointing.

However, a four-goal 15-minute blitz in the rematch with the Red Devils proved exactly what this team can do.

It would be weird if Spain, the newly crowned world champions, weren't at the top of this list.

Sitting at the summit of Nations League Group A3 with a 100 percent record only solidifies the case.

Spain won four out of four games during the September-October international break, including another statement victory over England. Luis de la Fuente's side also picked up back-to-back wins against Croatia and comfortably dispatched Czechia.

Superstar Lamine Yamal racked up four goals in four appearances, while Mikel Merino continues to be a not-so-secret weapon off the bench, netting three in just 109 minutes of action.

While a lack of clean sheets across the four games will be a mild concern for a team that conceded just once in their entire World Cup-winning campaign, it's really the only thing to criticize Spain for—and the stakes weren't exactly high.

Right now, La Furia Roja are the best international team on the planet. Even with the 2028 European Championships nearly two years away, they are already comfortable favorites.

articles.title: Mikel Arteta: Arsenal boss signs new contract until 2030
articles.summary: Mikel Arteta says this is "only the beginning" of Arsenal's success after signing a new contract with the Premier League champions until 2030.
articles.body:
Manager Mikel Arteta says this is "only the beginning" of Arsenal 's success after signing a new contract with the Premier League champions until 2030.

BBC Sport reported earlier this month that an agreement had been made on an improved new contract.

The Spaniard's deal was set to expire at the end of this season, with his time in charge of the Gunners now possibly stretching to a decade following his arrival in December 2019.

Atletico Madrid boss Diego Simeone is reportedly paid over £20m per year, as was former Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola - both of whom Arteta benchmarked his worth against.

The new contract includes an increase from his current salary of £10m per year plus an additional £5m in bonuses.

"This club is unique, its character and the way it makes you feel, and I have a great sense of privilege that our journey together will continue," Arteta said.

"We have already built a special bond and created memories that will last a lifetime, and what is so exciting is that this is only the beginning of what we can achieve together."

The 44-year-old has won a Premier League and FA Cup in charge of Arsenal , losing the Champions League final against Paris St-Germain in May.

Guardiola's departure from City at the end of last term made Arteta the longest-serving manager in the English top flight.

And the Gunners' chief executive, Richard Garlick, believes that factor will provide them with a "competitive advantage over the other teams" in the league.

"Mikel is the only manager that's won the Premier League that's currently managing [in it]," he said.

"You look at all the other teams in the sort of traditional top six, and they've all gone through managerial changes.

"We've now got a manager who's been with us for a significant period of time and has been allowed to build and develop a team over a period of time.

"The excitement now is we see [the] platform that we've got and we build from there."

With Arsenal targeting a period of sustained success, Garlick added: "We can't stand still. We can't sit there, pat ourselves on the back, and say job done.

"This is the beginning, not the end of our journey. This is where we want to go on and show the confidence that that win is going to bring to us.

"We want to dominate football for the next number of years. We're in a really strong position to do that, but we need to keep finding that edge that gives us that advantage."

Arteta wants to build a dynasty - analysis

News of Arteta's new deal at Arsenal won't come as a shock.

The fact his previous deal expired at the end of the season did put a slightly greater emphasis on the speed of discussions than normal.

But Arteta has been transparent about his desire to stay at the club beyond the end of this campaign.

Dynasty building is what has driven Arteta's decision. Winning Arsenal 's first Premier League title in 20 years last season is viewed as just the start.

Coming within a penalty kick of winning their first Champions League trophy came as a gut-wrenching blow - but also a huge motivation.

"We share a special bond with Mikel. We are so proud of everything we have achieved since he returned to the club in 2019," co-chairmen Stan and Josh Kroenke said.

"He has a deep understanding of Arsenal 's values and carries them in his heart. He knows what this club means to everyone connected to it and is committed to building on everything we have achieved together."

With that in mind, there was never a sense Arteta was preparing to walk away from the team he has built to become one of the best in European football.

So with a deal for their manager to stay now agreed, the foundation of Arsenal 's recent revitalisation into a footballing force remains in place.

Does more history beckon? Arteta is committed to finding out.
