articles.title: Thomas Tuchel: England 2.0 - what has Three Lions boss changed?
articles.summary: What has Thomas Tuchel tweaked as he looks to refine his England blueprint rather than rewrite it from scratch?
articles.body:
After the World Cup, Thomas Tuchel was asked whether he had seen his version of England during the tournament - a question that drew a hesitant and unsure answer.

Over the summer, the Three Lions found ways to win but often leaned on scrappy moments of brilliance rather than methodical dominance.

Tuchel had in mind the type of team, the tactics and the patterns he wanted to see.

He and his assistant coach Anthony Barry have often spoken about borrowing ideas from the Premier League.

Building up short. Enticing pressure. Playing quickly across the middle of the pitch – whether through powerful carrying or long balls – to find runners in attack against fewer defenders.

These were all ideas England tried to execute, to varying levels of success, in the World Cup.

During the recent international break, many of the ideas we saw during the World Cup and prior have persisted.

There have, however, been deliberate changes in tactics and personnel, with the 53-year-old Tuchel looking to refine his blueprint rather than rewrite it from scratch.

England have continued to focus on first playing short from the back, intent on drawing opponents towards them before speeding up play to find their attackers in space.

Rather than giving the build-up responsibilities to two central defenders and a holding midfielder as they did during the World Cup, England have committed an extra player to this central build-up unit.

Two central midfielders and two central defenders look to solve problems against pressing attackers with a shape that fluctuates between a 2-2 or a 3-1.

Tuchel has praised Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott, who took turns with Myles Lewis-Skelly to pair with Elliot Anderson in the heart of midfield in Declan Rice's absence.

Either player taking the role of busy partner for Anderson - boasting technical quality and an ability to take turns playing as a lone holding midfielder - have proved successful for England.

Anderson, who sat at the base of midfield for much of the World Cup has, as a result, been deployed in a more varied role.

With Scott or Lewis-Skelly picking up the ball from the centre-backs, Anderson has dropped to form part of the back three alongside Marc Guehi and Ezri Konsa.

This has given him time and space on the ball, facing forward, allowing him to use his forward passing to find attackers quickly.

Anderson has also found himself higher up the pitch on occasion, with the protection of his midfield partner behind him, allowing him to showcase his attacking quality.

An interesting knock-on effect of this, and a nod to England's overarching evolution, has been the intensity England have shown as they have attacked.

"We've always played with high energy and a very aggressive style off the ball, to press high," Tuchel explained. "Now we have added another layer.

"[Now, our] intensity was very high on the ball. We did a lot of high intensity runs, a lot of counter movements, and invested a lot in counter pressing.

Anderson's ability to counter-press is an individual example of this improvement but more collective changes have contributed to England's increased intensity in possession.

In the World Cup, the system looked like a 4-3-3 on paper.

The two centre-backs and holding midfielder formed a triangle. On both flanks, a central midfielder, full-back and winger formed a triangle. Harry Kane took a roaming role.

These wide triangles were the main method of chance creation. Key to this was constant movement as England looked to make it hard for opponents to track them.

Although this often got England's winger one-against-one, teams could match England man for man in the wide areas, especially as they fatigued and off-ball runs that rid them of their markers became less common.

England's recent 3-1-3-3 shape in possession has given them an extra player at the back but appears to have also provided better attacking dynamics.

The wide centre-back has contributed to attacking play out wide. England's full-back, winger and number ten work together and are often also joined by one of the strikers or holding midfielders.

These five players have given England a numerical advantage on the flank. This has mainly been seen down England's left.

Defensively, this provides them extra players around the ball, capable of counter-pressing with more intensity to win the ball back quickly.

Offensively, this has given them an unmarked player or two that they have often found well. By overloading the left flank, England pull opponents towards one side which has also enabled them to switch it to the opposite side for team-mates in space – often two against two.

Lewis Hall has stood out in this system, displaying a great chemistry with former club team-mate Anthony Gordon. Hall has taken a wide position frequently, allowing his winger to move in-field playing closer to the striker.

Tuchel highlighted England's 'counter-movements' as part of their improvement and the swapping and replacing of zones between Hall and Anthony Gordon have been a good example of this.

The best example, however, has probably been in the form of Kane and Gordon.

The Barcelona winger hugged the touchline for much of the World Cup, being released in behind before crossing it, rather than finding space in the box.

England's wide overloads and Hall's role have resulted in Gordon playing more central for longer parts of the game, allowing him to work more closely with Kane.

With Kane dropping deep, defenders are pulled out of position, a trigger which Gordon has used brilliantly to make runs the opposite way.

The use of runners attacking space Kane creates is not new - Jude Bellingham and Morgan Rogers have previously found joy exploiting it, but Gordon has been the latest beneficiary, while starting out wide.

Gordon's narrow runs from a wider starting position have been mirrored by Saka and Rogers on the other side too - a new string to England's attacking bow.

Trent Alexander-Arnold started against the Czech Republic, and took a wider position for large parts of the game that moved Saka almost permanently into a inside-right position.

From here, he appeared dangerous and provided goal threat while Alexander-Arnold assisted Gordon with a cross from out wide.

Despite this, the Real Madrid man was benched for Jarrell Quansah against Croatia with the pair starting together against the Czech Republic on Tuesday.

If asked to summarise Tuchel's England in one idea, runs off the ball would be a good answer. Perhaps this is why Trent Alexander-Arnold has found it difficult to find a place in Tuchel's squad.

"Trent is a unique player," Tuchel said. "He is not a runner.

"He is not someone who runs through the last line, who does overlaps [and] underlaps. [Saka and Trent] need to find a way to not be too static. On the right side, [we need] movement through the last line - to play with dynamic movement."

Against Croatia, Saka similarly found himself in central areas when Quansah held the width but played as a winger when Quansah moved centrally.

In both cases, Quansah was sure to make repeated runs beyond his winger.

Irrespective of his running, Alexander-Arnold's display on the ball across both games caught the eye. And when it comes to off-ball movement, he has shown promising signs.

For other coaches, that alone may have guaranteed him a starting spot in future but what is evident is that for Tuchel, there are underlying principles that take precedence - ideas we have seen him look to implement since his appointment.

In the past, England were accused of being a team of world-class individuals without a system.

Tuchel, more than ever, is looking to land on a world-class system.

It is up to the players to convince him of their role in it, even as it evolves.

articles.title: Chelsea: Xabi Alonso must solve long-standing defensive issues and needs Moises Caicedo fit for key run of games
articles.summary: Chelsea's Xabi Alonso era stalled with just one point from their final three Premier League games before the international break; On a special podcast ahead of their return against Bournemouth on Saturday, we examine the long-standing issues Alonso must solve and why Moises Caicedo is key
articles.body:
The new Blues boss will need to solve two key issues to turn that narrative around in a key run of games coming up.

That was the verdict from the latest Sky Sports Premier League podcast assessing Chelsea's start to the season under their new boss.

Chelsea's defence - which has conceded more goals than any other side so far - and their midfield - struggling to control games without injury-hit Moises Caicedo - were two areas in the spotlight.

Ahead of Chelsea's return to action against Bournemouth - and with Everton (a), Spurs (h), Liverpool in the Carabao Cup (a), Man Utd (h), and Sunderland (a) before the next international break - Sky Sports News reporter James Savundra outlined the issues. And how Alonso could solve them…

A defensive solution and midfield audition?

"The defensive issues that Chelsea have had pre-date Alonso's arrival. It is now 21 Premier League matches since they last kept a clean sheet which is remarkable - even though Chelsea have had a huge amount of change and there's been a huge amount of transition in 2026. For a club the size of Chelsea that simply isn't good enough.

" Emi Martinez , it felt like a no-brainer when they signed him, because of the issues they've had over the course of the last year few years when it comes to that goalkeeper situation but also there was an acceptance I think from most football fans that Emi Martinez isn't at the level that he was two or three years ago. Now clearly there's a period of adaptation which is taking longer than he and Chelsea would have hoped and perhaps he'll get back to that level which we've seen over the course of the last year. This is a World Cup winner he played in the World Cup final only a few months.

" Maxence Lacroix made a huge amount of sense as well in terms of bringing in an experienced defender who has still got the ability to get better but what has not helped Xabi Alonso is the number of injuries he's had. He's chopped and changed a little bit when it comes to that back line. I think the favoured backline, the favoured back three will be Wesley Fofana , Levi Colwill and Lacroix. But already Colwill, who I thought was really impressive in the FA Cup final when he came back from injury, he has struggled somewhat on the left-hand side of defence with Lacroix playing deeper in terms of that back three.

" Josh Acheampong there needs to be a role for him as well. Chelsea fans want to see him in the starting XI. But you can't win anything if you don't have a strong core and the goalkeeper has struggled a little bit at the start of the season the backline isn't quite where it needs to be and the midfield is nowhere near right now.

" Moises Caicedo has only played 14 minutes in the Premier League this season and the midfield has changed every single week, culminating in what we saw on Friday Night Football - nobody would have predicted this - Jordan Henderson's first appearance in a Chelsea shirt, starting in a Premier League match against Brentford alongside Valentin Barco .

"I think Chelsea will look very different moving forward when you have Marco Palestra fit - he was really impressive in pre-season playing as one of the wing backs - and Caicedo alongside a midfielder.

"You feel like between now and January it's going to be a case of which midfielder can audition the best and prove to the Chelsea ownership group and to Xabi Alonso that they don't need to sign a midfielder in this transfer window.

" Romeo Lavia you could say that has been a real pro, the fact that he's remained fit and he has completed matches. But he didn't feature in that game against Brentford, so can you rely on him? Reece James , unfit once again. The dream scenario would probably be Caicedo alongside James but saying that, James has shown already this season that he still needs to learn that role because the goal that Martin Odegaard scored for Arsenal was all about James not tracking the runner. There was another game against Leeds where he failed to track his runner as well. So he's still learning the role.

"But things will look much better when everybody's fit and there is a real patience from everyone at Chelsea, from Xabi Alonso, from the ownership group that this will take time."

articles.title: Ver al Barça en directo en la Champions sólo cuesta 7,5 euros, pero el partido es en... Bakú
articles.standfirst: El encuentro de la fase de la liguilla es el 25 de noviembre
articles.summary: El encuentro de la fase de la liguilla es el 25 de noviembre
articles.body: El Barça puso hoy miércoles, a las 10.00 horas, las entradas a la venta, para los socios, del encuentro de Champions League contra el Sabah, que los de Hansi Flick disputan el próximo 25 de noviembre. El precio de los tickets es de sólo 7,5 euros. El compromiso continental se disputa en Bakú, Azerbaiyán. El Barcelona puso hoy a la venta los billetes para el partido europeo. El club informó, a través de sus canales, que para efectuar la compra de entradas para asistir al encuentro de la fase de la liguilla de la Champions League será necesario que los socios interesados completen a través de la web oficial del Barça el formulario de reserva que el club ha preparado a tal efecto. Quedan exentos, además, los socios menores de 6 años, los que en el momento de la celebración del partido no tengan 6 meses de antigüedad, los sancionados por la Comisión de Disciplina y los que tengan algún importe pendiente de pago. El proceso de compra, condicionada a la disponibilidad de los billetes, se inició hoy a las 10.00 horas y finalizará a las 23.59 del día 18. El Barça, que ambiciona esta temporada conquistar la Champions League recuerda, así mismo, que en este caso no ofrecerá desplazamiento. El encuentro, correspondiente a la quinta jornada de la fase de la liga, se disputará el próximo 25 de noviembre en el Baku Olympic Stadium a las 18.45 horas (hora peninsular española). El Barça goleó al Feyenoord en el primer cruce de la Champions League: se impuso por 5-1. La próxima semana, el día 13, juega contra el Galatasaray en Turquía en el primer desplazamiento continental de este curso. El 20, los los de Hansi Flick juegan en París, el 3 de noviembre reciben al Aston Villa y el 25 tienen el encuentro en Azerbaiyán, cuyas entradas se pusieron esta mañana a la venta para los socios.

articles.title: Rafita eclosiona ahora para Europa
articles.standfirst: El canterano del Málaga se pone en el escaparate mundial
articles.summary: El canterano del Málaga se pone en el escaparate mundial
articles.body: Rafita no deja de crecer. El lateral del Málaga se ha convertido también en una de las sensaciones de las categorías inferiores de España después de aprovechar a lo grande una oportunidad que, en principio, no estaba en sus planes. La lesión de Javi Hernández abrió la puerta de la sub 21 de David Gordo y el futbolista de Torre del Mar entró en la convocatoria por la gatera. Después, sobre el césped, se ha ganado por méritos propios seguir dentro del radar de La Rojita. No es algo nuevo en su trayectoria. Hace justo un año, por estas fechas, fue una plaga de bajas en los laterales del primer equipo del Málaga la que permitió a Rafita estrenarse de la mano de Pellicer. Ahora, su crecimiento ha ido mucho más allá. Sus dos titularidades con España y, especialmente, su actuación ante Rumanía sub 21 junto a Pablo García, futbolista del Racing, han servido para poner todavía más focos sobre un jugador que ya era seguido por buena parte del fútbol profesional. Rafita ha demostrado que puede competir al máximo nivel internacional y esa exposición también tiene consecuencias en su valor de mercado. El Málaga tiene en sus manos una pieza muy cotizada: un futbolista capaz de desenvolverse tanto en el lateral derecho como en el izquierdo y que ofrece alternativas en una posición cada vez más demandada. Una auténtica perla defensiva de la cantera blanquiazul. El canterano tiene contrato con el Málaga hasta junio de 2029, pero su cláusula de rescisión no está acorde con la dimensión que empieza a adquirir su figura. Radio MARCA Málaga ya avanzó en agosto que el club de Martiricos trabaja en una mejora de sus condiciones. La intención pasa por premiar su evolución y, al mismo tiempo, elevar su cláusula para protegerse ante el interés de otros clubes de LaLiga. Ese interés ya existió el pasado verano. Osasuna y Betis preguntaron por la situación del jugador, aunque Rafita, como el resto de sus compañeros, no quiso escuchar propuestas para abandonar La Rosaleda. El Málaga desea ahora acelerar la mejora de su contrato antes del próximo parón internacional de noviembre. Si mantiene este nivel, todo apunta a que David Gordo volverá a contar con él. Y eso, además de ser una buena noticia deportiva, puede hacer que la lista de pretendientes siga creciendo.

articles.title: Mikel Arteta contract: Arsenal boss signs new deal to extend stay at Premier League champions
articles.summary: Mikel Arteta has signed a new contract at Arsenal; Arteta had entered the final year of his previous deal but now extends his stay at the Emirates Stadium; the 44-year-old is already the longest-serving manager in England's top-four leagues after his appointment in 2019
articles.body:
The 44-year-old's existing contract with the Premier League champions, signed in September 2024, was due to expire next summer.

But the Spaniard, who was appointed in 2019, has committed his future to the club until June 2030.

Arteta has transformed Arsenal's fortunes during his tenure and guided the club to their first Premier League title in 22 years last season following three straight second-place finishes.

He also led the Gunners to only their second Champions League final, which they lost on penalties to Paris Saint-Germain. He has also won an FA Cup and three Community Shields.

"It's a privilege to commit my future to the club and to continue to work with exceptional people who want the best for Arsenal," Arteta said in a statement.

"This club is unique, its character and the way it makes you feel, and I have a great sense of privilege that our journey together will continue.

"We have already built a special bond and created memories that will last a lifetime, and what is so exciting is that this is only the beginning of what we can achieve together.

"I'm extremely grateful to Stan and Josh for their trust and support, and feel honoured to be leading this club through such a special period in its 140-year history.

"This is such a proud moment for me and my family. I feel the love and respect from our fantastic supporters, and they have mine - and ours - in return."

Meanwhile, Arsenal chief executive Richard Garlick said: "This is an important time in Arsenal Football Club's history. We want to create a winning era together with Mikel.

"We will continue to work hard together as we aim to fulfil our long-term ambitions for the club and our supporters.

"Mikel has the belief, determination and the understanding of what it takes to build something remarkable and enduring here, and we are excited to continue that journey together."

Only four managers - Sir Alex Ferguson, Pep Guardiola, Jose Mourinho and Arsene Wenger - have won the Premier League title more than once.

So can Arteta join the esteemed list? His new contract gives him a chance to build an Arsenal dynasty. Sky Sports' Nick Wright assesses his chances of doing it.

Sky Sports News reporter Gary Cotterill:

"Arsene Wenger certainly got off to a faster start, didn't he? But Arteta has got the time to do it.

"Arteta now, he's on his fourth contract and he's 44 years old. Arsene Wenger was 47 when he arrived at Arsenal. So he's already got a lot of years on him.

"In three years, Arteta will have been at Arsenal for 10 years, but still be the same age that Wenger was when he was appointed at Arsenal.

"I think that will be one of his ambitions, because people still think about Wenger as being the best manager, certainly modern manager, that Arsenal have ever had.

"And Arteta is certainly in the running, given his age and the fact that they seem to be having this contract situation, which doesn't look like it's going to stop anytime soon, to get the trophies that Wenger got."

articles.title: Mikel Arteta's new contract: The challenges facing Arsenal boss as he enters 'step five' of his project
articles.summary: As Mikel Arteta, already the longest-serving manager in English football, signs a new contract at Arsenal, we assess his reign so far and outline the challenges ahead, including another potential rebuild; plus, how is he similar to Jose Mourinho?
articles.body:
In a special podcast, Ron Walker is joined by Gary Cotterill, Nick Wright and Sam Blitz to discuss Arteta's new deal in detail. The panel reflect on his tenure so far and look at the challenges ahead as he aims to build an Arsenal dynasty.

Nick Wright: "The club is unrecognisable from 2019, on and off the pitch. It's been a collective effort but Arteta is the driving force behind it. He's one of few constants over these six or seven years.

"He has brought the club back to the elite. This is a team winning titles now, also consistently reaching the latter stages of the Champions League. Obviously, there are still imperfections. There's still fallibility. The Brighton game showed that.

"But what made that defeat such a surprise was that it was so uncharacteristic, and that tells you a lot about the standards that he has set. Arsenal hadn't lost a game by three goals in the Premier League for over three years. It just doesn't really happen.

"And it's what we've come to expect, that capacity to deliver consistently. They have become so difficult to beat. And remember, Arsenal used to get bullied and beaten up all the time.

"It's a total transformation of their identity under Arteta. They are defined by that competitiveness. They are a super-competitive team, they are relentless, and that's a reflection of the manager.

"These are the things that define him, and these are the ways in which he has imprinted his own personality on this team. The team is very much a reflection of Arteta and the way he approaches his job."

Sam Blitz: "It's been well-documented that when Arteta arrived, he had a five-step plan to bring Arsenal to the top of English football.

"Step one was creating that culture. There was that infamous story of the first-team meeting with the Arsenal players, where the players walked in and the room was a mess.

"Chairs and tables were everywhere and Arteta said, 'this is what English football thinks of you, and we're going to fix it bit by bit'.

"Step two was probably getting the right players in. We saw that with the likes of Gabriel joining, Ben White, Aaron Ramsdale. These are more the profiles of what he wanted.

"Step three then was to challenge, and that coincided with the time when Gabriel Jesus and Oleksandr Zinchenko arrived. Arteta said those two 'changed our world', so that got them challenging for the top honours once again.

"Step four was to win, to get over the line. That also coincided with the arrival of Win the dog, who is a popular figure at the training ground. And that obviously happened last season.

"And now we've got to step five, which is the D-word. Anyone associated with Arsenal will know the D-word is dynasty. And it's interesting that this new contract coincides with that step five."

Gary Cotterill: "Arsene Wenger certainly got off to a faster start, didn't he? But Arteta has got the time to do it.

"Arteta now, he's on his fourth contract and he's 44 years old. Arsene Wenger was 47 when he arrived at Arsenal. So he's already got a lot of years on him.

"In three years, Arteta will have been at Arsenal for 10 years, but still be the same age that Wenger was when he was appointed at Arsenal.

"That will be one of his ambitions, because people still think about Wenger as being the best manager, certainly modern manager, that Arsenal have ever had.

"And Arteta is certainly in the running, given his age and the fact that they seem to be having this contract situation, which doesn't look like it's going to stop any time soon, to get the trophies that Wenger got."

Sam Blitz : "The potential rebuild will test Arteta.

"If he's still in charge of Arsenal in 2029, he will have overtaken Jurgen Klopp's spell at Liverpool. If he's in there in 2030, he will have overtaken Pep's time at Manchester City.

"Arteta is younger, this is his first job and he's probably got more in the tank compared to those two. But it's the rebuilds that really damaged Klopp and Guardiola.

"If you actually look at the ages of the Arsenal squad, come 2029, you'd have Gabriel, 31, [Martin] Odegaard, 30, [Declan] Rice, 30, [Kai] Havertz, 30, [David] Raya, 34.

"Those are five players you'd probably put at the very heart of this Mikel Arteta project. All of them would probably have to be thinking about moving on.

"Does Arteta have that in him when he gets to that stage to then really go and create a new team, almost?"

Nick Wright: "The attack is the area where fans want to see the most improvement but there is a slight misconception around Arteta in terms of what he wants the team to be and who he is as a manager.

"People are sometimes critical of Arsenal for putting too much emphasis on set-pieces and being too defensive. They did lean into those things to win the title, no doubt about it.

"But that was largely to do with injuries. When you can't get your most effective attacking players on the pitch, it's hard to be that free-flowing force. He maximised their chances of winning by leaning into other things.

"You have to remember, the last time he had Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Odegaard fit for a full season, Arsenal scored a club-record number of goals with 91 - more goals than any Wenger team.

"He would like to return Arsenal to that level of attacking potency. I don't think he's wilfully turned them into something else. He has adapted. He is pragmatic."

Gary Cotterill: "They are both ruthless. This is the biggest thing they have in common. Arteta was ruthless when it came to Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus.

"Jose Mourinho has been ruthless with players as well.

"If they're not doing the job or around the place that they were brought in to do because of age or attitude, no matter what relationship they have, Arteta will ruthlessly get rid of them.

"He's ruthless when it comes to the officials as well. Arteta is becoming like a mini-Mourinho in his criticism of decisions and referees."

articles.title: Josan Ferrández, detenido tras una denuncia de su pareja por presuntos malos tratos
articles.standfirst: El capitán del Elche CF está en dependencias judiciales de Orihuela a la espera de que se determine su situación
articles.summary: El capitán del Elche CF está en dependencias judiciales de Orihuela a la espera de que se determine su situación
articles.body: Josan Ferrández, futbolista y capitán del Elche CF, ha sido detenido tras una denuncia presentada por su pareja por presuntos malos tratos, según ha adelantado este miércoles el diario Información. El jugador permanece en dependencias judiciales de Orihuela mientras se determina su situación. Josan, que fue además pregonero de las últimas Fiestas de Agosto de Elche, y su pareja tienen dos hijas en común. Ambos se encuentran en proceso de separación, según la información publicada por el periódico. La denuncia incorpora varios elementos De acuerdo con Información, la denuncia incluye diferentes elementos, entre ellos mensajes de WhatsApp presuntamente vejatorios y fotografías de hematomas que la denunciante atribuye a los hechos denunciados. El procedimiento deberá esclarecer ahora las circunstancias de la denuncia y determinar las posibles responsabilidades que puedan derivarse. El futbolista mantiene la presunción de inocencia mientras continúa la investigación y sigue en dependencias judiciales de Orihuela a la espera de conocer su situación. Ante las informaciones que han trascendido en las últimas horas sobre nuestra situación personal, queremos manifestar conjuntamente que nos encontramos inmersos en un proceso de divorcio. Como ocurre en cualquier proceso de estas características, estamos atravesando momentos que no siempre son sencillos. No obstante, queremos dejar claro que mantenemos el respeto muuto y nuestra voluntad de afrontar esta situación de la manera más respetuosa posible. En relación con las informaciones y especulaciones que se han generado, queremos señalar que, en este momento, no existe ningún procedimiento judicial abierto que afecte a Josan Fernández. Por respeto a nuestra situación personal y, especialmente a nuestro entorno más cercano, pedimos que cualquier cuestión relacionada con este proceso permanezca dentro de nuestra esfera privada. Nuestra voluntad es zanjar cualquier tipo de polémica y poder afrontar esta nueva etapa con respeto y normalidad. Agradecemos la comprensión y el respeto hacia nuestra privacidad.

articles.title: El Madrid C no sale del atasco
articles.standfirst: Sigue sin ganar tras cinco partidos y se mantiene en puestos de descenso
articles.summary: Sigue sin ganar tras cinco partidos y se mantiene en puestos de descenso
articles.body: El Real Madrid C no sale de su atasco de fútbol y resultados y ya son cinco partidos sin ganar, con un balance de tres empates y dos derrotas que lo mantienen en los puestos de descenso. El segundo filial blanco recibía hoy al Guadalajara en Valdebebas en el partido aplazado, por la Intercontinental que disputó el Madrid en septiembre, y a la quinta tampoco fue la vencida. Carlos Díez adelantó a los blancos de penalti en el primer tiempo (el primer gol de la temporada para los de Marc Carrasco) y los visitantes empatarían en la recta final del partido, poco después de que el Madrid C se quedase con 10 tras la expulsión de Camara por doble amonestación. Marc Carrasco volvió a mover el once inicial, con las grandes novedades del central juvenil Mateo Garrido y Melvin, con el objetivo de dar con la tecla y encontrar una versión competitiva del equipo. Pero el escenario sigue sin cambiar. El mal comienzo no ayuda a un filial falto de confianza y, sobre todo, de fútbol. Propone demasiado poco para encontrar el premio del triunfo. Aún así, se encontró con el penalti sobre Mateo Garrido al filo del descanso que transformó Carlos Díez. Un golpe de confianza y de tranquilidad del que no sacaron provecho. Tras la reanudación, el Guadalajara se adueñó del partido, comenzó a llegar con insistencia y encerró a un Madrid C superado y que se cargó de amarillas, lo que tuvo la consecuencia de la expulsión de Camara a 10 minutos del final. El Guadalajara acabaría encontrando el premio a su insistencia con el gol de Bautista e, incluso, pudo llevarse el partido tras estrellar dos balones en el palo. Real Madrid C: Illia; Melvin, Mateo Garrido, Ariel, Lezcano; Beto, Camara; Carlos Díez, Lacosta, Manex; Fran Santamaría. También jugaron: Álex Pérez, Bailón, Gabri Valero, Barroso y Castrelo. Guadalajara: Josele; Eimil, Ablanque, Babin, Sergi Segura; Miki, Morillo, Robles, I. González, S. Miguelez; Roni. También jugaron: Batán, Bautista, Bonilla, Juancho y Dani Martínez. Goles: 1-0 (49') Carlos Díez, de penalti; 1-1 (83') Bautista.

articles.title: England: Thomas Tuchel still stinging from World Cup criticism despite Nations League positives
articles.summary: Thomas Tuchel gave a spiky response to questions about how England's World Cup exit to Argentina has been portrayed; England had just beaten Czech Republic to all-but guarantee a Nations League quarter-final place following a third-place finish in the summer
articles.body:
Some 83 days after England succumbed to Argentina in the World Cup semi-final, we'd moved on.

And then Tuchel showed that he hasn't, and revealed his underlying bitterness and hurt.

The England boss is clearly still smarting from the vociferous criticism that came at him from all angles following the World Cup exit. And now, when all had been forgotten, if not forgiven, it was Tuchel who brought the subject back up.

He'd made it very clear at the start of this extended international break that he wanted to look forward rather than back. We know that he'd had clear-the-air talks with the England players who had lingering anger at his public criticism of them and their sub-standard 'DNA', but Tuchel stressed it is now all about the bright new future, with an assault on the Nations League trophy and, ultimately, the Euros in two years' time.

But, feeling re-emboldened after a very positive autumn for his England team, he bit back at those pesky journalists who'd dared to question whether he got the tactics wrong when 1-0 up and close to reaching a first World Cup final in 60 years.

Asked whether he'd seen an improvement in mood, confidence and momentum since the end of the World Cup, he replied: "Yeah, I do. It's necessary to move on and I can only repeat: we didn't go out in the group stage. It often feels like that. But we didn't."

A follow-up question asked him whether he felt the scrutiny and assessment of England's World Cup exit had been too harsh, and Tuchel's response was pointed and said with a scornful tone and a stern expression.

"In between, it felt a little bit like it, yeah. (Why?) Why? Were you in the press conference before the France game? (Me? No, I wasn't there.) Yeah. You would have known why."

The tense exchange came after a three-week camp where sources had told Sky Sports News just how positive the mood had been, and how optimistic the players and staff are about what lies ahead. Tuchel and the squad were as one again, the "Brotherhood" Tuchel craved, back together again.

And yet the image that Tuchel portrayed to the outside world, whenever the cameras were on him at training or in the regular news conferences that came with four games in 11 days, was one of a brooding malaise.

I'm told the England boss became aware of his less-than-positive demeanour and made a conscious effort to change for the latter stages of the camp, and in fact the Tuchel on the touchline at Wembley on Tuesday night was back to his animated, tactile, positive self.

Until the post-match news conference. Where it looked the opposite. And it was very surprising that the England boss decided to take that tack.

Satisfaction and clarity from latest camp

That media moment aside, Tuchel can look back on this extended international break with a lot of satisfaction. He engineered by far the best performance and result of his tenure with the 7-0 obliteration of Croatia on Saturday, and he has what he would call "proof of concept", in the sense that England showed an energy, a ravenousness for the ball, and a relentless attacking intent which the England boss has been calling for from the moment he took over.

Even the defeat to Spain in the opening game came with a great deal of positives, with England matching their opponents in many areas, and they were perhaps a slipped penalty kick away from victory over the world champions.

Most impressive was England's front four, who Bukayo Saka told me is the best in the world when they are on song. Kane told us there is a new freedom and fluidity in the way they play together which brings out the best of all of them, and makes it much more challenging for opposing defences. When he drops deep, others (often Jude Bellingham ) run beyond him to fill the void; when Bellingham goes wide to exploit space, Anthony Gordon or Saka will drift inside. Tuchel's assistant, Anthony Barry, described it by saying they'd let Bellingham "out of a cage" and that they were reaping the rewards.

A number of new players put their hands up to be England regulars too. Alex Scott was name-checked by Barry as someone who is already considered part of the inner sanctum, and Lewis Hall showed that he is probably first choice left-back now, after some hugely impressive performances throughout. Trent Alexander-Arnold , too, reminded everyone of his world class ball skills - whether he did enough to impress Tuchel for a regular return to the England fold remains to be seen, when all of the other injured right backs are available again.

It felt like there is more clarity too on some of those players on the England fringes, and who missed this camp. Cole Palmer was given some Tuchel tough love, when the German coach said he'd missed too many opportunities to be in camp. Phil Foden wasn't mentioned at all, after he'd been overlooked in the original squad selection. Harry Maguire likewise, after voicing his frustration at being left out of the World Cup squad.

You also get the feeling that, in the debate around who will ultimately replace Kane as England's No 9, Bellingham is looking more and more likely. It was noticeable that the Real Madrid master often filled in there in this camp, rather than Tuchel turning to Dominic Calvert-Lewin on the bench.

Tuchel now has a month-and-a-half to reflect. He can be very pleased with the direction of travel. But the next stern test is as tough as it gets: Spain away, in November.

articles.title: Una cláusula del miedo en un puesto peliagudo
articles.standfirst: Salinas no podrá jugar contra el Espanyol
articles.summary: Salinas no podrá jugar contra el Espanyol
articles.body: Salinas será baja ante el Espanyol. El lateral no podrá enfrentarse al conjunto perico por la conocida como ‘cláusula del miedo’, una condición incluida en su cesión y que le impedirá disputar el encuentro del viernes. Es una fórmula que se popularizó especialmente en el fútbol español a raíz de varios casos protagonizados por futbolistas cedidos por el Real Madrid, como Munitis, Morientes o Eto’o, que terminaron haciendo daño al conjunto blanco cuando se midieron a su club de origen. En el caso de Salinas, la condición fue una petición expresa del Espanyol que el Málaga aceptó dentro de las negociaciones por la cesión del futbolista. El club blanquiazul asumió esa limitación para poder avanzar en otros términos del acuerdo. Una situación diferente a la de Dotor, cuya cesión desde el Celta no contempla esta prohibición. Por tanto, Salinas tendrá que vivir el duelo desde la grada de La Rosaleda. Su ausencia obliga ahora al Málaga a buscar soluciones para el lateral izquierdo. Carlos Puga aparece como una de las opciones más claras, mientras que Rafita también está llamado a tener protagonismo. El problema es que el canterano afrontó este martes su segundo compromiso con la selección española Sub-21 y llega a Málaga con apenas una sesión de trabajo antes del encuentro frente al Espanyol y 160 minutos extras a su espalda. El desgaste y el poco tiempo de recuperación introducen un pequeño condicionante en la preparación de los blanquiazules, aunque Rafita parte con muchas opciones de ocupar el carril izquierdo ante el conjunto perico. La tercera vía es Adam Aznou. El futbolista catalán todavía no ha podido estrenarse con el Málaga después de sufrir varios problemas físicos desde su llegada. Su falta de ritmo competitivo convierte su posible presencia en el once en una incógnita. El cuerpo técnico deberá comprobar durante las próximas sesiones en qué condiciones se encuentra y si está preparado para asumir de entrada la responsabilidad en un partido de tanta exigencia.

articles.title: Los precios para el Nou Mestalla oscilan entre los 300 y los 1.700 euros
articles.standfirst: El club considera que solo un 20% de los socios notarán una subida importante en los pases del nuevo estadio
articles.summary: El club considera que solo un 20% de los socios notarán una subida importante en los pases del nuevo estadio
articles.body: El Valencia ya ha puesto en marcha el traslado al Nou Mestalla. El club ha publicado los precios de los cerca de 50.000 abonados en los que se pondrá el tope. La estimación del club es ingresar unos 38 millones de euros en este concepto, un 50% más que en la actual temporada. En el nuevo estadio pagará todo el mundo sin tener en cuenta la edad. El proceso de traslado tiene tres fases. La creación de grupos para ir con tu gente más cercana (del 14 al 30 de octubre), la selección del asiento (a partir del 17 de noviembre) y por último la formalización (el pago será en verano). Los precios del nuevo estadio permanecen más o menos estables. El suelo de precio es de 300 euros y el techo alcanza los 1.700 euros, siempre al margen de los asientos de Hospitality. Más de 40% de los asientos abonables tendrá un precio menor a 500 euros. Cuanto más centrado y más bajo será más caro. Estos precios, que se pueden consultar en su totalidad en la web del club se establecen sin aplicar los determinados descuentos por antigüedad y asistencia. Se prevé que el descuento medio por persona será de un 15%. En la Grada Superior (13.922 localidades) los precios van de los 300 y los 450 euros. En la Grada Alta (13.922 localidades) los precios oscilan entre 400 y 650 euros. En la Grada media, los precios varían entre los 1.100 euros y los 600 y por último, en la Grada Baja (la más cara), los precios van desde 750 a 1700. Uno de los datos en los que insiste el club es que la media ponderada lleva los precios del nuevo estadio a un 10% más baratos que en el Mestalla actual. La realidad es que hay zonas, más altas, en las que el abonado podrá acceder por menos de 500 euros, en total más de 40% del estadio nuevo. Los abonados que más van a notar el incremento serán cerca de un 20% que se sitúan frente a tribuna en el viejo Mestalla. Allí habrá aumentos de más de 800 euros por el abono ya que se considera esa zona igual que la tribuna en la que se sitúa el túnel de vestuarios y los banquillos. Grada visitantes La grada visitante tendrá algo más de 850 entradas y estará delimitada por una valla trasparente algo que facilitará la venta de los asientes cercanos a dicha grada en la que se colocaran los hinchas del equipo visitante. En partido europeo se irá al 5% del aforo total y por tanto se irá por encima de las 3.000 butacas. De hecho, la UEFA, en caso de competición europea bloquea 5.340 butacas por todo el estadio. Estos asientos bloqueados más los compromisos de club, más el hospitality llevan los asientos bloqueados a más de 14.000, por lo que el máximo de abonados generales será de 56.000 socios. Grada de animación La grada de animación va a crecer en algo menos de 400 aficionados. No ocupará las 7.000 localidades de todo el fondo. El precio para la grada de animación pasa a 340 euros sin descuentos. El precio sube 30 euros con la diferencia de que en el nuevo estadio estarán cubiertos. Esta grada sigue con su límite de edad para nuevas altas y estará situado en la grada baja Norte del estadio. Elegir el asiento de forma presencia El club ha habilitado en el campo de Mestalla una sala en la que cuando los abonados, uno por grupo, que quieran sacar el abono para el nuevo estadio podrán probar los asientos y tener de forma telemática, a través de una herramienta de 3D, la visión real desde cada una de las butacas.

articles.title: The lesson Cristiano Ronaldo can still learn from Lionel Messi’s heroic goodbye
articles.summary: Whereas Lionel Messi has ended his national team career as a hero to many, both in Argentina and abroad, Cristiano Ronaldo is staining his legacy with Portugal.
articles.body: Saying goodbye is never easy. Within a sporting context, the hardest farewells often come when it’s time for players to retire, but such decisions are often more complex than you’d imagine – fraught with ego and identity dilemmas for athletes who have been consumed by their sport for so long. But regardless of how hard it is to let go, there tends to be a right and a wrong way of going about it. Take Lionel Messi for example. Following defeat in this summer’s World Cup final, the Argentine captain penned a handwritten letter explaining his decision to step down from the national team. In it, the 39-year-old said the decision hurt his “soul” but thanked teammates, coaches and family for joining him on the ride. Part of him stepping aside was to let a new generation come through behind him and he promised to support the team with the rest of Argentina from now on. Then, last night, Messi said goodbye for real after being convinced to play one more game for La Albiceleste. Thousands of his followers flocked to Buenos Aires to celebrate a player who has become nothing short of a deity in the country and a goal and two assists in a 3-0 win against Benin seemed a fitting way to end a stellar 20-year international career. Tears were flowing from the moment he stepped out for the warmups to the moment he addressed the crowd with a near 10-minute speech at the end. Nothing is perfect, but Messi trudging off the pitch in the famous sky blue and white stripes while surrounded by an adoring stadium crowd seemed as good as it could get. I think we can all agree that this is a good example of how to say goodbye. Then, we have Cristiano Ronaldo. Night and day On the same day Messi went out in a blaze of glory, the Portuguese captain posted a rather bizarre statement on social media which felt as strange as it did sad. In it, the veteran forward explained his recent decision to walk away from Portugal’s UEFA Nations League training camp, feeling aggrieved that new head coach Jorge Jesus had broken alleged assurances regarding playing time and not given subsequent public apologies for reneging on said assurances. Basically, long story short, it kind of all boils down to Ronaldo not playing 30 minutes at the end of Portugal’s win against Norway on October 4 – shock, horror. As a result, the current captain stormed away in a strop that seemed to throw his future with the national team into question. But, in that public post on Tuesday, Ronaldo promised to come back, urging the Portuguese FA to punish him for his actions. Yet his whole statement felt like a “sorry, not sorry” that you’d expect more from a jilted teenager than you would from one of the greatest players in the history of the Beautiful Game, and the worst thing about it is I’m not sure many people really care at this point – certainly fewer than Ronaldo imagines. Yes, his Instagram post with his statement earned over 15.5 million likes, but that’s far from his top post even in the last few months. A modern-day Greek tragedy Ever since he struggled through the 2022 World Cup, it was clear Ronaldo could no longer have a telling impact on the international stage. But his influence over what happens with the team is so big that the striker has continued to play and weigh down what could have been a golden generation for the country. This summer’s World Cup simply solidified what most people already thought: that Portugal was better off without Ronaldo. But try telling the five-time Ballon d’Or winner that… Instead, Ronaldo continued to play in North America, shouting “I’m back” into the camera lens after scoring two goals against tournament debutant Uzbekistan in what could be the cringiest moment of the tournament. Retiring from the national team seemed to be an option after that World Cup disappointment, but Ronaldo said he was urged to continue by the Portuguese soccer federation president – something which now looks incredibly ill-advised. Now, the aging superstar finds himself in an awkward situation where no one wants to be – overstaying his welcome like that uncle at Thanksgiving or Christmas who can’t read the room. What’s even worse is that his prolonged farewell has started chipping away at his undeniable legacy. Don’t forget that his incredible talent inspired his nation to victory at the European Championships in 2016, a moment that his country will never forget. But that was over 10 years ago, and his country is now better off without him – the eye tests of the team’s play on the pitch and the results prove as much. Ironically, it’s the irrefutable ego that made Ronaldo so good that is now leading to his downfall – a Greek tragedy Sophocles or Euripides would have been proud to write. Perhaps he’s stuck around so long because his old rival Messi has enjoyed so much success with Argentina in recent years, and he’s desperate to show the world one last time that he should be held in as lofty a pantheon as the Inter Miami forward. But comparing the two men today makes Ronaldo look worse than he may realize. It’s now time for him to say goodbye to the national team. Doing so quickly might still enable him to have a farewell like Messi in Buenos Aires. Most people seem to know it – except, it seems, Ronaldo himself.

articles.title: Are away ticket prices too expensive? And is a price cap on the agenda?
articles.summary: Scotland's top flight is the best attended in Europe per head of population. But does the rising cost of going to games put that status at risk?
articles.body:
An adult Kilmarnock supporter heading to Ibrox on Saturday will be asked to hand over £34 to watch their team.

Hibernian fans eager to be at their new manager's debut match at Tannadice will have to part with £30. Dundee punters at Falkirk will have to pay £28, as will St Mirren followers at Tynecastle.

All that before you factor in travel, food and whatever else comes with a day at the football.

Further down the SPFL, the entry fee drops. But Morton fans could still pay £24 at Arbroath in the Championship; Hamilton supporters £21 at Alloa in League 1; and Kelty Hearts followers £18 at Stirling Albion in League 2.

So how much is too much for a match ticket?

The SPFL regularly trumpets the fact that Scotland's top flight is the best attended in Europe per head of population.

But does the rising cost of going to games put that status at risk? What can we learn from elsewhere? And what - if anything - might change?

We asked all 42 SPFL clubs how much they charge visiting supporters and below are the figures that they provided. Within each of the four divisions, prices for adult tickets are broadly similar between the different clubs.

The graphics below capture the most expensive and the cheapest price at each ground, with the actual figure changing based on the opponent, location in the stadium, and whether the ticket is bought in advance.

A greater variation comes among concession prices, with many clubs offering free child entry with a paying adult, among other deals.

The graphs do not shown these promotions, but rather the range of prices for any kind of individually-bought ticket.

Aberdeen fan Glen Schreuder: "I'd like to see an away ticket cap. One of the reasons I don't do much away travel anymore is because it is becoming unaffordable with the rise in not just ticket prices but general prices."

Celtic fan Paddy Loughran: "Fans should be in unison in trying to put this argument to the league. I think there should be a bit more of a unity here and making sure we are holding the right people accountable."

Dundee fan Ethan Hampton: "I really like how there is an away-day culture in British football. You want it to stay intact but how much more can you ask of supporters when they are bleeding themselves dry to follow their team? In England, they can maybe take the hit on ticket prices, but Scotland is not the same."

Dundee United fan Paul McNicoll: "The cost of away tickets is borderline scandalous - some of the venues are a lot higher than others. It would be good if there was standard price, but it feels like we are miles away from that."

Falkirk fan Grant Heaney: "Away ticket prices are excessive. I think there definitely has to be some sort of cap introduced. I can see both sides of it - everything is going up in price and clubs are obviously affected by that as well."

Hearts fan Greg Playfair: "If you cap away prices home supporters will say 'hold on, why is that supporter paying less than me? '. It is a tricky one."

Hibernian fan Matty Fairnie: "Some clubs try and keep the price down, but I think others just see the fans as a commodity to milk. Gate receipts are a huge part of the income for Scottish clubs so they would almost be turkeys voting for Christmas."

Kilmarnock fan Sandy Armour: "In the big wide world, everything else is going up in price. I would say try and limit it to £20. Maybe you could get six or seven clubs - the non-city clubs, shall we say - together and say 'how about we have an agreement between us?'."

Rangers fan Jamie Currie: "As someone who goes home and away, I find away pricing vastly overpriced given the product. It should be capped at £20 but it's the biggest earner for clubs so it's a catch 22."

St Johnstone fan Sam Miller: "It seems more expensive than it needs to be for what you are getting in return. I would suggest fans like myself don't understand the finances needed by a club to run it on a day to day basis. Maybe if that was made clearer, we would maybe be more understanding of why ticket pricing is what it is."

St Mirren fan Mark Jardine: "St Mirren mostly make our money from people coming through the door, so I understand why prices go up. But I think it will get to a point where you are putting people off. I do find myself siding more probably with the Twenty's Plenty, £25 cap side of things."

So a lot of fans in Scotland have suggested a price limit on away tickets and they don't have to look far to see one in operation.

A £30 cap has been in place in the English Premier League for the last decade and, in March, clubs voted unanimously to keep it in place for another two seasons.

It was introduced amid a recognition that ticket prices had become too high and that away fans were "essential for match atmosphere", according to the league.

Since its introduction in 2016, away attendances have increased from 82% to 91%.

Michael Brunskill of the Football Supporters' Association, told BBC Scotland there was initially some grumbling from home fans, who sometimes had to pay more but that the mood soon changed.

"The money clubs lost is minimal and the reason the Premier League engaged is that executives understood the arguments we were making. They came to the conclusion that marginally lower prices means full away ends. That means stadiums look fantastic on TV and more pies and pints sold as well, so it all added up."

Is something similar on agenda in Scotland?

Afraid not. A cap on away ticket prices is not on the SPFL's agenda and has not been discussed by the clubs any time recently.

Comparisons with England perhaps fall down when you consider that Scottish clubs are far more reliant on matchday revenue, given their smaller broadcasting deals.

Furthermore, despite the ongoing cost of living pressures, attendances in Scotland are continuing to rise so clubs will likely be reluctant to introduce a measure which - initially at least - could lead to drop in income.

The issue has attracted political interest, with the Scottish Green's calling for a £25 cap prior to the Holyrood election in May.

But, while a cap doesn't exist, those in power might point out that there is a safeguard on away ticket prices, with the SPFL preventing clubs charging visiting supporters more than home fans for equivalent seating.

A number of clubs offer various concessions and offers and it should be noted that away fans can attend games at various levels of the SPFL for less than £25.

The harsh reality is that the cost of everything seems to be going up at the moment and, perhaps, any campaign for cap will only gain real traction when fans stop going.

articles.title: Yan Diomande, por donde sea
articles.standfirst: El fichaje millonario del Real Madrid ha demostrado su peso ofensivo con Costa de Marfil por todo el frente de ataque y sigue pidiendo paso a Mourinho
articles.summary: El fichaje millonario del Real Madrid ha demostrado su peso ofensivo con Costa de Marfil por todo el frente de ataque y sigue pidiendo paso a Mourinho
articles.body: Yan Diomande ya está de regreso a Madrid tras jugar sus tres partidos con Costa de Marfil, dos de ellos de titular y un tercero saliendo desde el banquillo. El jugador se va a incorporar ahora a las órdenes de Mourinho tal y como se marchó, pidiendo paso para el once tras su última suplencia en el derbi. Otra certeza que ha dejado el fichaje más caro en la historia del Madrid es que no hace falta cambiar mucho el esquema del equipo blanco para darle paso. En los tres duelos con su país, ha jugado por la derecha (2-0 ante Ghana), donde lo ha hecho con Mou para no sentar a Vinicius, pero también brilló por la izquierda en el segundo duelo (0-2 contra Somalia) y en el último, ya amistoso, saliendo en la segunda parte jugando como segundo punta y en la única derrota (0-1 frente a Camerún). Diomande ya avisó en el Real Madrid de que su adaptación avanzaba ya se reflejaba en el terreno de juego. Pese a que Mourinho le dejó en el banquillo en el derbi, su papel de inicio ante Rayo y Elche fue de lo más destacado. Ahora el dilema tras el parón es cómo encajar al jugador de Costa de Marfil con Vinicius, Bellingham y Mbappé como intocables... a priori. Diomande está llamando a la puerta y no lo debe estar haciendo tan mal cuando su valor de mercado ha aumentado pese a que en el Madrid aún no es titular. En la revisión de este pasado lunes por parte del canal Transfermarkt, su valor asciende a 120 kilos, prácticamente lo que ha pagado el Madrid sin bonus. Su cotización anterior, de finales de mayo, aún en el Leipzig, era de 90 millones. En una encuesta de MARCA justo ante de comenzar con los partidos de selección, el 86% de la afición pedía con más de 50.000 votos la presencia del costamarfileño en el once. Y la mayor parte le veía en el puesto de Vinicius. El brasileño cuenta con la confianza del club y del entrenador pese a que en este parón no ha brillando en ninguno de los tres partidos. Pese a que por cifras es cierto que ninguno ha marcado ni ha asistido en los tres encuentros, la presencia y la influencia ha sido mucho mayor en el caso del africano.

articles.title: ‘Cristiano deserves the same’: Gary Lineker laments Ronaldo’s Portugal finale compared to Messi’s farewell
articles.summary: Former England striker Gary Lineker has expressed sadness over the way Cristiano Ronaldo’s international career appears to be ending, saying the Portugal
articles.body: Former England striker Gary Lineker has expressed sadness over the way Cristiano Ronaldo’s international career appears to be ending, saying the Portugal great deserved a farewell similar to the emotional scenes that marked Lionel Messi’s final appearance for Argentina.Ronaldo, 41, left the Portugal camp last week amid a dispute involving coach Jorge Jesus and subsequently issued a lengthy statement explaining his decision. Messi, meanwhile, signed off from international football with a memorable performance in Argentina’s 3-0 friendly win over Benin, scoring one goal and setting up two others in front of an emotional home crowd.The contrast prompted Lineker to reflect on how the two greatest players of their generation have approached the closing chapters of their international careers.‘Cristiano deserves the same’“I think it's a bit sad because he's been so great. And ultimately in five years, 10 years' time, no one will remember this. We'll just remember how great he was,” Lineker was quoted by Reuters as saying at the Leaders Week sports industry conference at Stamford Bridge.“But I think if you look at Messi's farewell, it was so beautiful. And I think Cristiano deserves the same.”Messi, 39, ended a 21-year international career with 126 goals, two Copa América titles and a World Cup triumph. His final appearance for Argentina turned into an emotional celebration as supporters bid farewell to a player whose relationship with the country evolved from years of intense scrutiny to widespread adoration.Ronaldo and Messi have been compared throughout their careers in the debate over the greatest player of their generation. Messi has won the Ballon d'Or eight times to Ronaldo's five, while Ronaldo remains Portugal's record scorer with 146 international goals.Lineker hails ‘incredible’ KaneLineker also praised England captain Harry Kane, who equalled the country's record of 125 international appearances against the Czech Republic and took his England goal tally to 91 during a 3-0 win.Asked whether Kane belonged among England's greatest players, Lineker said: “I think he'd have to be in that conversation. Probably along with Bobby Charlton and maybe even Bobby Moore. I mean, look at his record, he's incredible.”“He's not just a goalscorer either, he's not just a box player like I was. He's way more than that. He can drop deep, he sprays passes everywhere, he scores all sorts of goals, both feet, head, he's got everything,” he added.Lineker, who scored 48 goals for England, echoed the view that Kane's all-round contribution places him among the country's historic greats.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Dani Olmo: ni hay oferta ni atenderá al Bayern
articles.standfirst: El internacional está feliz en el Spotify Camp Nou y no contempla un cambio de aires
articles.summary: El internacional está feliz en el Spotify Camp Nou y no contempla un cambio de aires
articles.body: Dani Olmo es un jugador importante en la selección española y en el Barça. Atraviesa un gran momento que inevitablemente eleva su proyección y le coloca en el mercado. Desde Alemania, se insiste en el interés del Bayern de Múnich, que ya tanteó su fichaje cuando militaba en el Leipzig. Pero ese deseo recuperado no se ha concretado, al menos de momento, en ninguna propuesta que haya llegado al futbolista o al Barça. Y si lo hace, no será atendida. El centrocampista de Terrassa no tiene ninguna intención de abandonar el equipo azulgrana. Tampoco el club se ha planteado su salida. Olmo, de 28 años, lleva temporadas destacando en el fútbol y siendo uno de los centrocampistas más cotizados y codiciados. Algunos portales especializados le tasan en alrededor de 60 millones de euros, que es una cantidad muy similar a la que el Barcelona pagó por él al Leipzig en verano de 2024. En la Bundesliga brilló, como lo hizo en la competición croata cuando militaba en el Dinamo de Zagreb y como lo está haciendo en el Spotify Camp Nou. Ya suma 96 encuentros con la camiseta culé, en los que ha marcado 20 goles y dado 20 asistencias. El Bayern sabe muy bien de la calidad de Olmo porque lo sufrió en la Bundesliga, de hecho ya tanteó su fichaje entonces, y porque ha visto igualmente sus grandes actuaciones con el Barça de Hansi Flick y con la selección española, con la que ha intervenido en 59 encuentros: este martes sumará, si tiene minutos como todo parece indicar, el 60. Fue titular indiscutible en el pasado Mundial, que conquistó el combinado de Luis de la Fuente. El conjunto de Múnich, según insisten en Alemania, ambiciona fichar al profesional de Terrassa, que se mueve en la medular, la mediapunta y el extremo izquierdo. Lo tiene en su agenda para las próximas ventanas de mercado. De hecho, cuando estaba en el Leipzig ya fue tentado por el Bayern. Pero Olmo, con contrato hasta junio de 2030, no tiene pensado cambiar de aires. Ni el jugador, que es muy querido en el vestuario, ni el Barça están al corriente, de forma oficial, de ese interés del Bayern, aunque tampoco sorprende en los despachos culés, conscientes de la calidad y del cartel de su centrocampista. Pero ni el internacional, que alterna la titularidad en la mediapunta este curso con Fermín López y ha intervenido en los ocho encuentros disputados (7 de LaLiga y uno de la Champions League), se plantea una salida ni el club tampoco. Dani Olmo es feliz en el Barça y no se le pasa por la cabeza abandonar el Spotify Camp Nou. Quiere seguir sumando minutos y levantando títulos con el equipo de Hansi Flick.

articles.title: La Rojita asusta a Europa: "Cuando vayan siete, habrá que meter el octavo"
articles.standfirst: La España sub 21 de David Gordo cierra la fase de clasificación para el Europeo con 47 goles, cifra récord en la historia, apoyada en Los García: Pablo y Gonzalo
articles.summary: La España sub 21 de David Gordo cierra la fase de clasificación para el Europeo con 47 goles, cifra récord en la historia, apoyada en Los García: Pablo y Gonzalo
articles.body: Quien quiera entender a esta España sub 21 que se fije en una cuenta sencilla: cuarenta y siete goles en diez partidos. Nunca una selección había anotado tanto en una fase de clasificación al Europeo de la categoría, ni siquiera aquellos Países Bajos que llegaron a 46 camino de 2021. El equipo de David Gordo cerró su gira en Ibiza con un 7-1 a Rumanía que no solo valió el billete directo al torneo de Albania y Serbia, sino que sirvió para firmar la rúbrica de una fase de clasificación insultantemente prolífica. El festín tuvo su cima una semana antes, en Serravalle, donde San Marino encajó un 0-13 que se quedó a un solo tanto del récord histórico de la propia España, aquel 14-0 de 2005 que firmaron Iniesta, Silva y compañía. Aquella tarde, Carlos Espí se inscribió en los libros con cinco goles en un mismo encuentro, una marca que solo igualan el checo Chramosta y el serbio Kačar en toda la historia del campeonato. Tanto acumula esta generación que ha movido fronteras históricas. Con este arreón, España ha rebasado a Alemania como la selección más goleadora en la historia del torneo sumando fases de clasificación y finales: 628 tantos frente a 618. Adelantar a la Mannschaft en cualquier apartado del fútbol tiene siempre un sabor particular, y hacerlo en el capítulo de la pegada, terreno que durante décadas fue dominio germano, dice mucho del camino recorrido por el fútbol formativo español. Pero los récords son fríos si no tienen rostro, y el de esta Rojita es doble y comparte apellido. Los García. Pablo García, con ocho goles, y Gonzalo, con siete, escoltan en la tabla de artilleros a un Tresoldi que se les escapa por poco, y entre los dos sostienen buena parte de la pólvora del equipo. El extremo del Racing que firmó un hat-trick en Can Misses y el delantero del Fulham que respondió con un doblete. Un 'pique' con el que se ironizó tras el partido. "Aquí jugamos todos en equipo. Hoy ha metido Pablo tres, yo he metido dos, podría haber sido otro compañero. Lo más importante son los objetivos comunes", comentó el 7. En Gonzalo, el 'killer' de esta selección, late además una historia de reencuentro. Jugó en Ibiza como local, porque la isla le vio crecer: pasó por las categorías inferiores del Mallorca en su etapa de cadete, en Son Bibiloni, junto a Obrador, Luka Romero o Llabrés. "Recuerdo esa etapa como algo muy bonito y que me sirvió mucho", confesó. Su presente, sin embargo, mira a la Premier, y él mismo quiso leer su doblete en clave de club: "Espero que estos goles signifiquen poder sumar más empezando el sábado contra el Ipswich. Sigo adaptándome al Fulham y a la Premier". La otra mitad del binomio, Pablo García, llegó a la isla cargando una mochila de emociones más pesada. Hace apenas un mes salía llorando de la ciudad deportiva del Betis, el club de toda su vida, rumbo al Racing; anoche se marchó de Can Misses con un triplete bajo el brazo. "Me he apoyado mucho en la familia, en los amigos, en la gente que me quiere", explicó sobre esa montaña rusa. Y dejó una declaración de principios que resume el apetito de todo el grupo: "Si van 6-1, habrá que meter el séptimo; y cuando vayan siete, el octavo. Soy una persona muy ambiciosa, con mucha hambre de gol".
