articles.title: Spygate: Southampton boss Tonda Eckert keeps job after receiving six-week suspended ban and £28,000 fine
articles.summary: Southampton say Tonda Eckert's punishment "brings a conclusion to a regrettable period of our history”; Saints were expelled from the Championship play-offs in May after admitting to "multiple breaches" of unauthorised filming of their opponents' training
articles.body:
Saints were kicked out of the Championship play-off final and docked four points this term having admitted three breaches of EFL regulations after being caught snooping on semi-final opponents Middlesbrough and two other teams.

Eckert accepted full responsibility and was charged by the FA with three breaches of Rule E3.1 in relation to "misconduct", which hung over Southampton and their manager heading into the new campaign.

This ends 'regrettable period in our history' - Southampton

The German coach attended an FA hearing at the start of the international break and is able to continue his role against rivals Portsmouth this Sunday and beyond.

A statement from the governing body read: "Tonda Eckert subsequently admitted the charges, and an independent Regulatory Commission imposed a six-week suspension from all football and football-related activity, which is suspended until the end of the 2027/28 season, a £28,000 fine and a reprimand following a hearing.

"The suspended sanction will come into effect in the event he is found to have committed a breach of Rules or Regulations by requesting, authorising, taking, or using information from any observation of the training of another club, in whatever guise that observation may take."

The punishment is likely to draw strong opinions from across the game, with Southampton saying in a statement "this now brings a conclusion to a regrettable period of our history".

The club, who sit 13th in the Championship, say "measures have been put in place to ensure that such errors in judgement never happen again at our club" and they are "excited to move forward together towards a bright future".

Saints owner criticises EFL over Spygate handling

Southampton owner Dragan Solak said: "I'm pleased that the independent panel has come to a decision and that we have an outcome.

"We have already suffered enough, and we appreciate the panel's recognition of that.

"We are confident the manager has learned from this matter, and a suspended sentence allows him to continue in his role.

"I firmly believe that Tonda is one of Europe's most exciting young coaches, and with this distraction removed, I am confident he can lead the team to a successful season. I'd like to thank our fans for standing by us and showing the team so much support during a time when we have needed them more than ever.

"The FA process has been a positive experience. Tonda has been given the opportunity to be open and honest with the panel, and the panel has been able to see that he is simply a good person who made poor decisions.

"The same cannot be said for the EFL process, and the way they have subsequently treated us is not something we will forget.

"However, now is the time to look forward to what I believe will be a great future for our club."

Sky Sports News has approached the EFL regarding the Southampton owner's comments criticising the organisation's handling of the case.

The Southampton boss was charged by the FA with misconduct and potentially bringing the game into disrepute in July and later admitted to the charges.

The EFL expelled Southampton from the Championship play-offs in May and handed the club a four-point deduction for the 2026/27 season after they admitted "multiple breaches" relating to the unauthorised filming of their opponents' training, including before their semi-final against Middlesbrough.

Southampton beat Middlesbrough and were due to play Hull City in the play-off final before Boro were reinstated. Southampton appealed the decision, but the punishments were upheld by a League Arbitration Panel.

During the Spygate hearing, the EFL only had the power to charge clubs, not individuals. The FA waited for the EFL process to run its course before launching its own investigation.

In June, Eckert said he took full responsibility "for everything that happened", apologising to players, staff and supporters.

At that time, Southampton chairman Dragan Solak admitted Eckert had made a "mistake" but said the club was "fully behind him", reaffirming their target of winning promotion to the Premier League.

In the written reasons released following the League Arbitration Panel's decision to dismiss Southampton's appeal against their punishment, Saints' conduct was described as a "contrived and determined plan from the top down".

Eckert "loved" the information a junior analyst intern gathered when spying on one of his team's opponents, according to messages used as evidence in the hearing.

The written reasons detail how analysts felt pressure to carry out jobs asked of them as a colleague had lost their job earlier in the season.

The panel added: "A reprimand is considered appropriate because of the way in which junior members of staff were put under pressure to carry out activities which they felt were, at the least, morally wrong."

May 7: Middlesbrough make formal complaint to the EFL alleging a Southampton member of staff spied on their training session three days before their Championship play-off semi-final first leg.

May 9: Boro boss Kim Hellberg accuses Southampton of cheating after the first leg ends in a 0-0 draw at the Riverside Stadium.

May 12: Southampton charged with a breach of EFL regulations in relation to the spying accusations. Southampton request additional time to conduct an internal review.

The play-off semi-final second leg is played at St Mary's. Shea Charles' extra-time winner earns Southampton a 2-1 victory and a place in the Championship play-off final.

Emotional Hellberg hits out at "disgraceful spying", before Saints boss Tonda Eckert storms out of his press conference after being asked: "Are you a cheat?"

May 13: Photos allegedly showing the Southampton analyst near Middlesbrough's training ground released publicly.

May 14: It is announced the independent hearing to determine Southampton's fate will take place on or before Tuesday May 19. In a statement, the EFL say "the outcome of the disciplinary proceedings may yet result in changes to the fixture."

May 15: Middlesbrough publicly call for Southampton's expulsion from the play-offs. In a statement, they said: "In these circumstances, the only appropriate response is a sporting sanction which would prevent Southampton FC from participating in the EFL Championship play-off final."

May 18: Middlesbrough players return to training as the outcome of the independent disciplinary hearing nears.

May 19: EFL announces Southampton expelled from play-off final after hearing.

May 21: FA confirm they will begin their own investigation into Spygate.

May 23: Middlesbrough lose 1-0 to Hull City in the Championship play-off final.

June 1: WhatsApp messages reveal Eckert "loved" spying information despite the concerns of junior members of Southampton staff.

June 2: Eckert takes full responsibility for Spygate as Southampton owner Dragan Solak backs head coach.

June 17: Eckert tells Sky Sports News he received police protection amid threats during Spygate.

July 22: FA charges Southampton head coach Eckert with three breaches of rule E3.1.

September 25: Eckert is given a suspended six-week ban, running until the end of the 2027/28 season, and a fine.

'One of the most difficult moments in Southampton's entire history'

Analysis from Sky Sports News' Mark McAdam:

Southampton fans have been waiting for this news throughout the international break.

Remember, it was a couple of weeks ago where the FA sat down to go through all of the evidence and decide what sanctions - if there should be any - that will be meted out towards Tonda Eckert. The Southampton manger was involved in probably one of the most difficult moments in Southampton's entire history [and] probably one of the darkest moments in the club's history - and we know that Tonda Eckert was the head coach and was involved in this spying.

Now a lot of people thought this matter was closed, but the EFL can only sanction clubs not individuals. That's where the FA comes in and their hearing has been happening over the last couple of weeks.

What we know is that Tonda Eckert has a six-week suspended ban - he can still operate as normal. However, if there are any further rule breaches [and] he does anything at all which is not in the rulebook, this will be imposed. He's got a £28,000 fine and a reprimand.

He has broken rules, he's faced his punishment, Southampton have been kicked out of the play-offs, and they had a four-point deduction this season.

This probably feels like a sensible decision from those that have made it, the FA Regulatory Commission.

This now brings to a close what has probably been the most difficult chapter in his life and certainly a very difficult chapter for Southampton Football Club.

articles.title: Do England have Harry Kane replacement - or is he yet to emerge?
articles.summary: Harry Kane's record-breaking England career can't go on for ever. But do the Three Lions already have a ready-made replacement?
articles.body:
Where would England be without Harry Kane?

With every record he breaks and landmark he passes, the question becomes increasingly difficult to tackle. But, now aged 33, there is a growing need for an answer.

The Bayern Munich striker became his nation's joint-highest appearance-maker on Tuesday at Wembley, netting twice in the 3-0 win over Czechia, taking his tally to 91 goals in 125 caps.

He is arguably in the form of his life. He won a league and cup double with Bayern last term - scoring 61 goals in 51 games for the German giants in 2025-26 - and he's among the favourites for the Ballon d'Or.

However, when the next European Championship kicks off in the summer of 2028, Kane will be 35. Alternatives and eventual replacements will surely be on the mind of whoever is at the helm then.

Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel said: "You will not get another Harry Kane, first of all. We look for different options and solutions."

So what are England's options in a world without him? Is the answer already in front of us - or could it be someone yet to even emerge?

Kane's rise from childhood keeper to equalling England cap record

England's greatest international? Kane is now a serious contender

'I like him as a nine' - new role for Bellingham?

Tuchel seems to think England may have an option within their ranks already in the guise of fellow superstar Jude Bellingham.

He shrugged off question marks over his place in the team ahead of the World Cup to quickly become a rival to Kane as England's most influential player.

"I like him as a nine," Tuchel admitted ahead of England's 7-0 win over Croatia. "He is a natural goalscorer and he has the hunger to be on the scoreboard.

"He wants to be there and have the decisive action, so it makes not a huge difference if he plays as a nine or a 10.

The German has certainly helped Bellingham add a productive edge to his game.

Since the start of the 2026 World Cup, the Real Madrid star has netted 10 times in 12 matches for England, having scored six times in the 48 games beforehand.

BBC Radio 5 Live's senior football reporter Ian Dennis said: "The person who is going to replace Kane has already emerged – and that's Jude Bellingham.

"We have seen it at times, when they play that false nine, Bellingham can go into that advanced role. He will also eclipse Kane in terms of appearances. This is a player who will continue to go from strength to strength."

At Real Madrid, Bellingham played frequently as a false nine in his first season for the club, with Vinicius Jr. and Rodrygo offering penetration from the wide positions.

It was Bellingham's most productive season for Real Madrid, with the numbers indicating just how much of an all-round package he's developed into now.

In a similar style, so much of Kane's good work for England comes from dropping deep, operating as a playmaker and then surging into the box to finish chances.

If England want another player who can straddle the No. 9 and No. 10 positions simultaneously, then Bellingham could be their best fit.

And, with the likes of Phil Foden, Cole Palmer, Morgan Gibbs-White and Eberechi Eze, there are no shortage of options to fill the Bellingham role.

However former England goalkeeper Paul Robinson said on 5 Live: "He is not a nine, Bellingham plays off others.

"I do think if England are going to play this system – and remember Kane has a long time left – I don't see Bellingham as the out and out number nine."

Bellingham unlocks new level and potential to be 'one of the greatest'

In terms of natural centre-forward replacements for Kane, England do not have much depth.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin has made a case to be Kane's back-up. He has 17 goals in 40 Premier League appearances since moving to Leeds United last summer.

However, there is a sense that Calvert-Lewin is not a dependable finisher - he underperformed by 2.13 in terms of xG in the Premier League last season - while at 29 he is not a long-term solution to Kane.

Away from the Leeds striker, there are not many centre-forwards making a case.

The only other English strikers to score in the Premier League so far this season are Nottingham Forest's Liam Delap, rebuilding his career after a difficult spell at Chelsea, and Ipswich Town's Chuba Akpom, who both have one goal each.

Across the 2026-27 season, English left-backs, with six, have more goals than English centre-forwards, with five.

Danny Welbeck was pushing for a recall last season with 13 Premier League goals but at the age of 35, his time is likely to have passed and he is certainly no long-term solution.

Ivan Toney and Ollie Watkins, previously considered by Tuchel, are both playing their football in the Saudi Pro League and were both left out of the most recent squad. Both are also already into their thirties.

If England do have an issue at centre-forward due to a Kane injury or suspension - or his eventual retirement - they could always opt to play without one.

Tuchel has used the tactic before, with Kai Havertz often deployed at the point of the attack during his time as Chelsea boss. Havertz scored 10 goals in the 33 league games in which he was used as a centre-forward by Tuchel.

A more fluid system has also been used to great effect by world and European champions Spain, who have deployed converted wingers Mikel Oyarzabal and Ferran Torres as strikers.

Anthony Gordon, who scored three times during the international break, could fit that particular bill. The winger was used as a striker by Newcastle United late last season and had success in the Champions League, netting 10 times in 12 appearances overall.

Who could be the next striker to break through?

There are some intriguing centre-forward options coming through.

Aston Villa's 17-year-old striker Brian Madjo scored five goals in pre-season for Villa, including one in the UEFA Super Cup against European champions Paris Saint-Germain, bullying the elite centre-back duo of Marquinhos and Willian Pacho throughout.

Madjo has been sidelined for seven weeks since that game because of injury, but he is close to making a first-team return after appearing in a friendly against Sevilla during the international break.

In the Championship, 21-year-old Will Lankshear - a Tottenham academy graduate like Kane - has hit the ground running for Middlesbrough with eight goals in 11 appearances for his new club.

Man City's Divin Mubama, on loan at Southampton, has scored five goals in 10 European under-21 Championship qualifiers, while the likes of Bristol City's Dom Ballard and Millwall's Josh Coburn are seen as young strikers with huge potential.

And Kane could yet give them time to develop having been inspired by the longevity of the newly retired Lionel Messi.

"As you see on the other end with Leo there, he's still performing at the highest level," Kane said after England's semi-final loss to Argentina in the summer. "So I never want to put a limit on these things."

England supporters will hope so. So will Tuchel. That way, the Kane conundrum is likely to be passed on to one of his successors.

"There will be someone else, but it will not be Harry or a copy of Harry," Tuchel added. "We will find a solution when it comes to it but maybe not me. It might be another 10 years."

articles.title: Nolaskoain: "Me siento muy bien de central"
articles.standfirst: El guipuzcoano podría estrenarse en una convocatoria para Oviedo
articles.summary: El guipuzcoano podría estrenarse en una convocatoria para Oviedo
articles.body: El regreso de Peru Nolaskoain cada vez está más cerca. El futbolista de Zumaia lleva trabajando al mismo ritmo que sus compañeros desde hace una semana y acumula sensaciones positivas con el paso de los días, hasta el punto de que tiene muchas opciones de formar parte de la expedición que viaje este domingo a Oviedo. Después de seis meses en el dique seco por un esguince de tobillo, Nolaskoain valora entrenar como uno más y ahora quiere recuperar el nivel que tenía antes de lesionarse. "Ha habido días muy feos, que venía a entrenar y era igual que el anterior e igual que el siguiente. De esas también se aprende. Hay que trabajar, hay que hacer lo que depende de uno y he hecho lo que dependía de mí. Ha llegado el momento de sentirme bien otra vez y volver a disfrutar entrenando", reconoce con brillo en los ojos. La cuenta atrás para volver a competir ya está activada. "Creo que cogeré la forma rápido. Estoy como un niño de cinco años con un Chupa Chups en la mano. Tengo muchas ganas de volver porque me fui en un momento bueno personal y del equipo, y ver al equipo ahora con 21 puntos de 24 posibles y no poder estar ahí, me ha hecho volver más rápido todavía", confiesa. Nolaskoain estrenará dorsal en una declaración de intenciones de la zona del campo en la que más cómodo se siente. "Me lo he cambiado porque verme de central con el 8 no me gustaba nada estéticamente. Ahora mismo me siento muy bien de central. Creo que estaba en un momento bueno y yo creo que tengo que alargarlo y acostumbrarme a ello", explica. El ex del Athletic disfruta del momento colectivo, aunque mantiene la tranquilidad. "Si bajas al vestuario y preguntas, nadie te va a decir que estamos crecidos. Al igual que has ganado siete partidos, te pueden venir siete en los que no ves puerta y no ganas. Estamos mentalizados y tranquilos. No es casualidad que ganes siete partidos seguidos en esta categoría, pero yo gané siete partidos un año también y terminó como terminó", reflexiona sobre aquel descenso con el Deportivo.

articles.title: UEFA football leaders meet to shape strategy to oust FIFA’s Infantino
articles.summary: European football leaders gather in Berlin with the aim of shaping strategy to oust Gianni Infantino as FIFA president.
articles.body:
European football leaders were gathering Wednesday with time pressing to find a candidate and shape their strategy for trying to oust Gianni Infantino as president of FIFA.

UEFA has called its 55 member federations to a previously scheduled summit on Thursday in Berlin that arrives in the midst of European efforts to get a new leader for football’s world body.

Infantino’s divisive World Cup private investment plan – that failed within days of being revealed in July – pushed UEFA to act on longstanding mistrust of its former employee’s increasingly executive presidency at FIFA.

UEFA’s longer-term plans include preparing a criminal complaint against Infantino in Switzerland for possible financial mismanagement in the World Cup sell-off deal. It has asked courts in the United States to authorise discovery of evidence .

“Somewhere along the way things went too far with FIFA, and we’re looking to put things back where they belong,” UEFA general-secretary Theodore Theodoridis said last month.

Europe’s 55 count for more than a quarter of FIFA’s 211 member federations that can vote in the election on March 18 in Rabat, Morocco. Research by The Associated Press news agency suggests Infantino already has about 90 votes pledged – albeit before any potential opponent is known.

Still, UEFA is not a united bloc. Infantino has support promised from Azerbaijan, the home country of a close aide, and Latvia. On Wednesday he met with football and government officials in the Czech capital Prague.

First, UEFA and its allies worldwide need to agree on at least one candidate to challenge Infantino by the November 18 deadline to enter the race.

Which football leaders have been seen as potential candidates?

UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin was joined in August by his fellow FIFA vice presidents from Asia and North America in denouncing Infantino for deception and breach of trust over the World Cup sell-off plan.

Still, neither Ceferin nor his counterparts at the AFC and CONCACAF, Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim Al Khalifa of Bahrain and Victor Montagliani of Canada, currently look set to be on the FIFA ballot.

Ceferin has long dismissed any talk of himself running to lead FIFA, though he said last month at UEFA meetings in Greece there were “many, many” potential candidates.

Montagliani is expected to focus on his own re-election at CONCACAF in February.

Sheikh Salman has been Infantino’s FIFA election opponent before. He had been favourite in a five-man campaign that Infantino eventually won in February 2016.

Speculation has often pointed to Paris Saint-Germain president Nasser Al-Khelaifi, a close ally of Ceferin. The Qatari member of UEFA’s executive committee ruled himself out last week at a meeting of the influential European Football Clubs group he leads.

Infantino is part of UEFA’s focus in Berlin for the biennial business meeting of top executives from its member federations, which can debate policy, strategy and international football competitions.

The meeting is expected to discuss proposals for a more transparent FIFA and a presidential candidate willing to commit to those reforms.

articles.title: A Infantino le sale el primer rival: Ramon Vega planea presentarse a las elecciones de la FIFA
articles.standfirst: Las candidaturas tienen que presentarse antes del 18 de noviembre
articles.summary: Las candidaturas tienen que presentarse antes del 18 de noviembre
articles.body: El suizo Ramon Vega, exinternacional con Suiza y ex de equipos como el Tottenham Hotspur y el Celtic de Glasgow, tiene la intención de presentarse a las elecciones a presidente de la FIFA que se celebrarán a principios de 2027. Vega, de 55 años, es la primera persona que se ha posicionado como posible rival de Gianni Infantino en estas elecciones. Infantino, pese a toda la polémica que ha suscitado su intención de vender participaciones privadas de la Copa del Mundo y de la cantidad de entes que han pedido su dimisión, declaró que se presentará a la reelección. Este exdefensa, con pasado en Suiza e Inglaterra y que vistió en 29 ocasiones la camiseta del combinado nacional, se retiró en 2004 y ha trabajado en el sector de las finanzas desde entonces. "Me presento para reunir a la familia del fútbol y llevar a cabo una reforma y una modernización de la FIFA, restaurar su estabilidad y su credibilidad y reconstruir la confianza que nuestro deporte urgentemente necesita. Me presento porque mi vida me ha preparado para ayudar a este deporte", dijo Vega en declaraciones recogidas por la cadena británica BBC. "El fútbol no pertenece a presidentes, confederaciones o administraciones. El fútbol va más allá de eso, es el deporte de la gente. La actual presidencia ha desmoralizado el fútbol. Ha dañado la credibilidad de la FIFA. Tenemos que parar esto y que no vaya a peor". Las candidaturas para estas elecciones tienen que presentarse antes del 18 de noviembre. La votación se producirá el próximo 18 de mayo en el congreso de la FIFA que tendrá lugar en Rabat (Marruecos).

articles.title: El nuevo mapa del Madrid: Vinicius cae, Diomande vuela... y Güler remata
articles.standfirst: Los movimientos del mercado dejan una nueva fotografía de LaLiga
articles.summary: Los movimientos del mercado dejan una nueva fotografía de LaLiga
articles.body: Hace dos años, Vinicius valía 200 millones de euros y era, junto a Haaland, el futbolista más valioso del mundo. Hoy está en 130. Mientras tanto, Yan Diomande ha pasado de 90 a 120 millones y Arda Güler ya alcanza los 100. El mercado empieza a reflejar un cambio en el Real Madrid, con los jóvenes ganando terreno y algunas de las grandes estrellas perdiendo valor. Y por encima de todos sigue Lamine Yamal, que conserva los 220 millones y mantiene a Mbappé a raya en la cima por el reinado en LaLiga. La subida de Diomande es la más grande de toda LaLiga: 30 millones de euros de golpe. El marfileño pasa a ser el sexto jugador más valioso del campeonato, pese a que no llega ni a los 300 minutos con el Madrid y sólo dos titularidades. Todavía no ha marcado, pero el derbi ante el Atlético dejó una de sus primeras grandes señales de que algo bueno se está cocinando por detrás. Los 120 millones tienen también otra explicación. Transfermarkt no valora únicamente lo que un jugador está haciendo hoy, sino también su edad, su potencial y lo que el mercado ha demostrado estar dispuesto a pagar por él. En Diomande, todas esas variables apuntan hacia arriba y de ahí su explosión en la última actualización. La trayectoria de Vinicius es justo la contraria. En octubre de 2024 llegó a los 200 millones, convirtiéndose junto a Haaland en el jugador más valioso del mundo. Venía de ser campeón de Europa, MVP de la Champions y ganador de The Best. Era el punto culminante de su carrera pese a que se le escapó el Balón de Oro. Dos años después está en 130 millones. Ha perdido 70 millones, aunque sus números no se hayan hundido. Marcó 22 goles y dio 19 asistencias en la 2024/25 y firmó 33 goles y 14 asistencias en la 2025/26. Su caída responde también a otros factores: el rendimiento colectivo del Madrid, sus actuaciones con Brasil y, sobre todo, la sensación de que está lejos de la versión que le llevó a ser el futbolista más cotizado del planeta. Entre medias aparece otro madridista que sigue ganando terreno. Arda Güler ya vale 100 millones, diez más que en la anterior actualización. El turco se ha convertido en uno de los grandes activos jóvenes del Madrid y su crecimiento ya no se limita a las expectativas. Así, el Madrid coloca a cinco jugadores entre los diez más valiosos de LaLiga: Mbappé (200), Bellingham (160), Vinicius (130), Diomande (120) y Güler (100). Pero la renovación de la jerarquía no significa que el Barça haya perdido la batalla en el mapa de valoración del fútbol español. Lamine Yamal continúa siendo el jugador más valioso de LaLiga, con 220 millones, veinte más que Mbappé y sesenta por encima de Bellingham. El extremo del Barça mantiene la valoración que alcanzó en verano y sigue siendo, con sólo 19 años, el futbolista con mayor cotización del campeonato liguero. Además, el Barça coloca a otros tres jugadores en el top 10. Pedri mantiene los 150 millones, mientras que Fermín vuelve a subir y alcanza los 110. Desde diciembre, el centrocampista ha pasado de 70 a 110 millones, impulsado por su rendimiento y su capacidad goleadora. También sigue entre los diez primeros Pau Cubarsí, con 100 millones.

articles.title: Oblak ‘regresa’ a la pelea
articles.standfirst: Ya está tercero en la clasificación del que sería su séptimo Zamora. El año pasado estuvo más lejos que nunca del premio que se llevó Joan García.
articles.summary: Ya está tercero en la clasificación del que sería su séptimo Zamora. El año pasado estuvo más lejos que nunca del premio que se llevó Joan García.
articles.body: Hace apenas un año, Jan Oblak recogía el galardón como portero menos batido de una temporada en LaLiga. El esloveno se convertía así en el único meta de la historia (desempataba con Valdés y Ramallets) que alzaba el trofeo que otorga MARCA en seis ocasiones. Un hito muy difícil de superar, un hito que puede tener continuidad esta misma campaña. Y es que, transcurridas siete jornadas, el 13 rojiblanco se ha aupado ya al podio del Zamora. Radu y Sivera con seis goles en siete duelos encabezan una tabla en la que el esloveno se sitúa en el último cajón con un tanto más encajado, los mismos que Vallés y Soria. Una pelea más que reñida en la que Oblak, viendo la evolución defensiva de los rojiblancos, tendrá mucho que decir. Los siete goles encajados (dos de ellos desde el punto de penalti) han llegado desde disparos dentro del área, mientras ha realizado 16 paradas (2,29 por partido). El regreso de Jan a la pelea por el trofeo se produce tras una temporada en la que no pudo pelear el séptimo galardón. Joan García se estrenaba en el Barça y el entramado defensivo de los azulgrana dejó al meta con un promedio de 0,7 goles encajados por choque, muy lejos del los 31 tantos recibidos por el segundo capitán del Atleti en 30 choques. La buena racha actual (un gol encajado en los tres últimos duelos) devuelve a Oblak a la primera línea de un trofeo que nadie ha ganado más veces que él. Algo que este curso parece más cercano repetir en especial desde la llegada del Cuti Romero para dar un salto de calidad a la zaga. A sus 33 años, y más allá de ganar el que sería el séptimo Zamora, Oblak quiere seguir engordando su palmarés a nivel de clubes. Llegó en 2014, acarició la Champions en la final de Milán dos años después y fue en 2021 donde conquistó su título más preciado: LaLiga. En este entorchado jugó un papel determinante, aunque su hambre de títulos sigue intacta cuando afronta la penúltima temporada de su contrato, que acaba en 2028. Habrá cumplido entonces 14 años que le convierten en una de las grandes leyendas de la historia de LaLiga y del Atlético. De momento, las siete primeras jornadas de esta Liga le sirven para volver a la pelea… del Zamora.

articles.title: National high school girls soccer composite rankings
articles.summary: Indiana continues to dominate the latest USA TODAY Sports composite rankings for high school girls soccer this fall.
articles.body:
The 2026 girls' high school soccer fall season is continuing to chug along.

Twenty-six states are in season for girls' soccer in the fall, while another 20 compete in the spring and five unique states play their season in the winter.

USA TODAY Sports has developed composite rankings , using polls from MaxPreps and United Soccer Coaches.

The top two teams in the country remain from Indiana entering the second composite ranking, with the state holding four teams total in the top 25.
